#1935. Tottenham look set to deliver after so many disappointments but Roberto De Zerbi's side need a nasty streak if they are to build on their momentum ahead of a daunting festive period, writes RIATH AL-SAMARRAI

By RIATH AL-SAMARRAI, CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 06:52 EDT, 1 November 2026 | Updated: 06:31 EDT, 2 November 2026

It was late on Saturday evening when Roberto De Zerbi relayed a few of the comments he had shared with Tottenham’s players at half-time in their 2-0 win over Crystal Palace. One of those remarks was indicative of how quickly things can change.

In the knowledge that his side were 45 minutes away from a rare spot in the upper portion of the table, he reminded them: ‘We can't forget where we have been two weeks ago. Two weeks ago, before the Coventry game, we were last in the table and we can't forget.’

With Tottenham, it is always prudent to know calamity is never too far away, but for the first time in two years, there is a gathering excitement at the club - in the crowd and the dressing room.

The win over Palace was assisted hugely by Jean-Philippe Mateta’s red card after 13 minutes, but Spurs have an uncanny knack of slipping on the easier opportunities. Not this time – goals from Archie Gray and Jan Paul van Hecke punctuated a dominant performance and a third straight win. Three managers and 616 days had expired since the last such streak.

But Spurs appear to be on the march and a promising season is belatedly taking shape. To finally deliver after so many disappointments, there are certain areas where improvements must follow…

Roberto De Zerbi reminded his players of where they had come from during their 2-0 win over Crystal Palace

That was De Zerbi’s own assessment of his frontline after a familiar shortcoming against Palace may have been concealed by the win. It was not lost on him that both of Tottenham’s goals were scored by defenders, nor that they had 34 shots to Palace’s two. As ever, Spurs had abundant creativity in their side but lacked a clinical edge.

De Zerbi said: ‘If we want to follow perfection, we have to be more nasty, no? That is an individual thing, because if I'm number nine, number 10, I want to score. But I can't say nothing.’

He later clarified that comment to encompass the whole side, but it was clear that the onus falls most on Dominic Solanke and Omar Marmoush.

In fairness to the pair, Palace defended so deep after Mateta’s dismissal that they had no space to operate, but one goal apiece this season is a poor return. Solanke, in particular, needs to do a better job of reading the movements and intentions of those around him – too often on Saturday he appeared a thought or two behind Mathys Tel and Mohammed Kudus, who both impressed in the more generous spaces out wide.

De Zerbi wants his side to develop a 'nasty' streak - particularly his attackers

Marmoush is an interesting case for De Zerbi. His mobility and technical ability are clear but he is yet to reveal his best position. On Saturday he was used as a No 10, having already been switched between roles on the left and up front. This experiment drew muted results.

It might be the case that a sustained run in one spot would be beneficial, but for now there appears to be confusion over where to use him. There is also a nagging thought that his best striking potential comes in a two-striker system, as shown in his most prolific period at Frankfurt, but that is not the way De Zerbi plays.

A significant improvement for Tottenham has come in midfield and, specifically, the pairing between Matheus Fernandes and Sandro Tonali.

Acquired at great cost, there was limited patience around the delivery of their impact, but time was always necessary, because De Zerbi’s system is notoriously complicated. In recent weeks, Fernandes and Tonali have shown signs that the penny has dropped on what they have to do.

This has been especially relevant in the instance of Tonali, who is very much the tempo-setter of the side on the ball and off it. On Saturday, he was excellent, or worth ‘double’ in the words of De Zerbi. There were times earlier in the season when he appeared disinterested, as if Tottenham was not the destination he had in mind, but his work rate was brilliant against Palace – he covered 12.3km, won all three of his tackles, and completed 93 per cent of his passes. He was all-action.

The same would be said for Fernandes, who covered 11.6km of ground and finessed a superb cross for Van Hecke’s goal. As a pair with Tonali, he was key to the pressing operation that limited Palace to a single counter-attack in the second half.

Mateus Fernandes (pictured) and Sandro Tonali have been huge boosts in the midfield

De Zerbi struck an interesting note after the game by alluding to the cohesiveness of his side and how it has changed on the pitch. Perhaps that relates to the recent team-bonding exercise in Marbella, but more likely they just needed time to understand the complexities of their manager’s demands.

‘I think even before the international break we were playing well,’ De Zerbi said. ‘We were playing maybe not 90 minutes, but many parts of the game we played very well. We didn't score. We conceded a stupid goal and then we lost energy. We lost spirit. We lost the right union between the players.

‘If we compare Tottenham before the international break and Tottenham after the international break, now we are playing as a team. Before the international break we were playing as many very good players, but not as a team.’

Archie Gray, for one, is getting to grips with the less familiar brief at right-back. The requirements to swap spots with Fernandes, overlap Kudus or hold the advanced position are mind-scrambling, but he has adapted well. His withdrawal at half-time against Palace was down to his first-half yellow card and doesn’t detract from a salient point – he can evidently be trusted to replace Pedro Porro, or at least give the latter scope for a breather.

Tottenham have an opportunity now. Their next four fixtures are Leeds, Ipswich, Sunderland and Fulham, with a nasty run waiting in December and early January.

If they can get something from Elland Road, the other three assignments present a rich opportunity for momentum before the tricky festive period.

One key area to improve in the short term will come against defensive sides who offer less space. That Spurs scored only twice from 80 per cent possession against Palace highlighted the issue.

De Zerbi said: ‘We are improving in the principle and the quality of play. Maybe we are not ready yet to play against such a low block but maybe in two or three months we will be.’

#1934. Ryan Giggs sends Max Dowman message to JJ Gabriel over Manchester United exit

Ryan Giggs has urged JJ Gabriel to reconsider his decision to leave Manchester United and believes the 16-year-old should follow Max Dowman’s pathway at Arsenal.

Gabriel, who turned 16 last month, informed United of his desire to leave Old Trafford in September and has not trained with the club since then.

The young forward has attracted interest from several clubs across Europe, however, he has now reached a verbal agreement to join Real Madrid.

Gabriel’s entourage are understood to have been unhappy with his first-team integration at United and wanted him to feature in a Champions League fixture against Sabah FK, as well as in a Carabao Cup tie against Brighton in September.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

Giggs, meanwhile, also began his career as a highly rated young prospect in United’s academy but did not make his first-team debut until the age of 17 under Sir Alex Ferguson.

The 52-year-old went on to become the most decorated player in English football history as he won 34 trophies during his 24-year career with United.

When asked about Gabriel’s situation in a conversation with Rio Ferdinand, Giggs stressed the importance of patience and believes Dowman, who was handed his Arsenal debut at 15 years and 235 days old in August 2025, is going through the correct development process under Mikel Arteta.

‘So far in his career everything is going fine, why would you disrupt that? You’re on the right track,’ Giggs said of Gabriel.

‘I trained at 15, I didn’t play for the first team until two years later so you have to have that patience that people just don’t seem to have at the moment.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘And believe it or not, first-team football for Man United is completely different to playing in the youth team, playing pre-season for the first team, it’s completely different. That first game, yeah, you might do alright, but you have to do it for 40, 50 games a season. You’re going to get injuries, loss of form, bad results, so you have to be patient.

‘If you’re on the right trajectory then just bide your time, no matter how good you are.

‘Max Dowman is unbelievable but he’s not playing for Arsenal at the moment.

‘I’m sure he’ll bide his time, I’m sure he’s getting impatient, but he’s not kicking off, he knows in a couple of years time he might be the main man for Arsenal.’

#1933. Fortuna Sittard vs Telstar - prediction, team news, lineups

By Adepoju Marvellous | 05 Nov 2026 12:26

High-flying Fortuna Sittard return to Eredivisie action this weekend, hosting Telstar at the Fortuna Sittard Stadion on Saturday.

The home side begin this weekend’s round of fixtures in sixth place with 19 points - 10 places and 10 points clear of the visitors.

A trip to Feyenoord, who had won three straight meetings between the teams, threatened to end Fortuna’s six-game unbeaten run, especially after Luciano Valente opened the scoring just before the hour mark. However, Shiloh ‘t Zand equalised with four minutes remaining to force a share of the spoils.

While some may argue the point flattered Danny Buijs’s men given their performance, it was a reward for their resilience, a quality they have displayed in abundance since a 5-1 drubbing at the hands of Ajax in mid-September.

Having collected just seven points from a possible 15 in Sittard-Geleen, Fortuna’s return to form still has room for improvement via consistent results at home. A 1-0 win over Excelsior in their last home outing suggests they are moving in the right direction.

Bottom of the league in average ball possession this term (35.7%), Fortuna remain a side best known for their off-the-ball work. They finished second-bottom in this metric last season, only ahead of relegated Heracles.

With each of their next six matches coming against teams currently below them in the table, Fortuna have an opportunity to build a sustained run of positive results and enter the second half of the season well positioned for a European push.

After almost three months, Telstar finally ended their wait for a first victory since beating NEC Nijmegen on the opening weekend, running out emphatic 4-2 winners over FC Utrecht in Sunday’s clash at BUKO Stadion.

The victory came at a crucial time for manager Henk Brugge, who was under increased scrutiny after his side were knocked out of the KNVB Beker first round by lower-league opposition Almere City just four days earlier.

Two points adrift of safety, another Telstar defeat this weekend could pile the pressure back on Brugge and their away record this season has been dismal, with just one win, four points, and four goals scored from five matches on the road.

However, De Witte Leeuwen are unbeaten in their last five trips to the Fortuna Sittard Stadion dating back to August 2014, and will draw confidence from their most recent trip in March, when they cruised to a 4-1 victory.

Facing a side with the best big-chance conversion rate in the division (76.9%), Saturday’s visitors will be wary of conceding too many opportunities, despite boasting a significant advantage in clear-cut chances created (23-10).

Rodrigo Guth and Lequincio Zeefuik both limped off with injuries in Fortuna’s last outing and are doubtful for Saturday’s clash.

This could open the door for Ivan Marquez and Kristoffer Peterson - both substitutes last time out - to come into the hosts’ starting lineup.

Twenty-one-year-old Gerald Alders has missed Telstar’s last three outings and remains a doubt for this weekend.

Patrick Brouwer and Rui Mendes were also absent against Utrecht, although the former is likely to return to action in Sittard.

Tyrone Owusu has scored five goals and provided one assist in his last five matches for the visitors, making the midfielder one to watch.

Fortuna Sittard possible starting lineup:

Branderhorst; Pinto, Van Ottele, Marquez, Hubner, Dahlhaus; Ihattaren, Descotte, Brittijn, ‘t Zand; Zeefuik

Koeman Jr; Peersman, Soualhia, Valk, Caschili; Rossen, Ahmed; Demircan, Owusu, Martha; Thorisson

Fortuna are playing their best football in some time, and that momentum makes them strong favourites to edge an out-of-sorts Telstar side.

We expect the home side to make light work of their visitors and head into the international break on a high.

AC Milan could sign another young defender for the first team in January, according to a report from Matteo Moretto.

As the winter mercato nears, Milan will be focused on adding a first-team defender to lessen the pressure on the current options. However, they will not only look for experience. Although Endrick is something of a middle ground, he’s still a player for the future, rather than being a finished product.

In other words, the signings may still be players with a ceiling, even if they are ready to make an impact.

This afternoon, Moretto provided an update on the situation involving Timmo Hardung, but that’s not all. In fact, he also gave some information on the January mercato, with the Rossoneri looking to sign a young talent from Belgium, as MilanVibes relays.

“AC Milan are looking to acquire a central defender and strengthen their defence with a new player. Gonçalo Inacio remains among the most popular players for January, especially for coach Amorim.

#1931. Richarlison grabs last-gasp winner for 10-man Spurs in fiery Chelsea friendly

Tottenham concluded their tour Down Under with a 2-1 victory over London rivals Chelsea at Accor Stadium in Sydney.

Sandro Tonali put Tottenham in front with a deflected effort before Estêvão equalised for Chelsea minutes later. Tottenham’s cause was not helped by a red card for Austrian defender Kevin Danso, who lasted just three minutes after coming on at half-time.

After making a mistake, Danso brought João Pedro down and was given his marching orders for denying a clear goal-scoring opportunity. Chelsea came close to taking the lead with their one-man advantage only for Tottenham goalkeeper Antonin Kinsky to make some crucial saves.Just as the game appeared to be heading to penalties, Richarlison scored on the follow-up after Jamie Donley hit the post in the final few seconds of added time.

Richarlison. 90+2. pic.twitter.com/VIOS4Jh7P2

Tottenham will take on Getafe and Hoffenheim back on home soil before taking on Brentford on the opening weekend of the new Premier League season.

Chelsea have four more pre-season games, including fixtures against Juventus and AC Milan, before travelling to Fulham in the opening Premier League game of the Xabi Alonso era.

Chelsea Sharman-Lowe, Palestra, Colwill (Acheampong, 80), Palmer (Kellyman, 80), Gittens (Tosin), Essugo (Walsh, 80), Pedro (Delap, 80), Hato (Anselmino, 62), Fofana (Sarr, 80), Estêvão (Satpayev, 70), Lavia (Nicoll-Jazuli, 46).Substitutes not used Watson, Curd, Subuloye, Emenalo, Kavuma-McQueen.Goal Estêvão (21).Tottenham Hotspur Kinsky, Robertson (Kyerematen, 72; Tingey, 90+1), Davies (Takai, 81), Van Hecke (Danso, 46), Gray, Gallagher (Hardy, 54), Tonali (Donley, 81), Bergvall (Hall, 72), Tel (Williams-Barnett, 76), Solanke (Richarlison, 46), Solomon (Moore, 67).Substitutes not used Dubravka, Scarlett, Russell-Denny, Melia, Yang, Ajayi, Byrne, Tye Hall.Booked Gallagher (10).Goals Tonali (17), Richarlison.Sent off Danso (49).

Possession: Chelsea 46%-54% TottenhamShots: 14-7Shots on target: 4-4Corners: 1-1

There is the final whistle and the 10 men of Tottenham snatch victory at the death with Richarlison scoring with seconds remaining.

In the final few seconds of the game, 10-man Tottenham win it. Donley’s shot from just outside the box hits the post and Richarlison follows up to score. It would have been a close call on offside if VAR was in use but it is not and Tottenham will take victory in Sydney.

Tottenham are being forced into a late change as Kyerematen, who come on for Robertson and nearly scored that wonder solo goal, is being forced off injured and is replaced by Tingey.

Delap is found in the centre of the Tottenham box with a cross from the right but the striker’s header from around the penalty spot goes wide and does not really trouble the target.

Initially, after Danso’s red card, Chelsea were in the ascendancy with a man advantage but Tottenham have dealt pretty well down a man.

Kyerematen nearly scores a quite sensational solo goal from inside his own half before driving forward. As he approaches the Chelsea penalty area, he tries to pick out the top corner and his effort comes off the top of the bar.

Xabi Alonso is making seven changes, yes seven, at once! That includes the likes of Delap and Tosin, who takes the captain’s armband.

The changes keep coming as Williams-Barnett replaces Tel for Tottenham.

A reminder that if the game is level after 90 minutes there will be a penalty shoot-out.

Roberto de Zerbi is making a double substitution as Tye Hall and Kyerematen replace Bergvall and Robertson.

17-year-old Satpaev, who hails from Kazakhstan, is replacing Estevao for Chelsea. Satpaev, who was at Kairat and turns 18 in 11 day’s time, scored the other day for Chelsea against Western Sydney.

Moore, who was on loan at Rangers last season, is replacing Solomon for Tottenham.

Robertson is so, so lucky. He is under no pressure as a cross comes over from the left and he should clear it with ease. However, he tries to be too clever and chests it back looking for his goalkeeper. There is not enough on it, allowing Pedro to nip in but his effort from inside the six-yard box is saved. Pedro probably should have scored and Robertson is a relieved man. Kinsky at the moment is the reason why Tottenham are not a couple of goals behind.

Tottenham have found it tough to get forward a lot since Danso’s red card but they do counter now and it ends with Tonali having a shot from just outside the box but his effort is easily saved by Sharman-Lowe.

Chelsea make a change as Anselmino comes on for Hato.

Palmer plays a ball down the right channel to pick out the run in behind of Palestra, who then returns it back to Palmer inside the Tottenham penalty area. Palmer’s first-time effort from the edge of the box is blocked.

Kinsky makes another big save to deny Chelsea. Tonali, who thought he had been fouled, loses the ball deep inside his own half, before Estevao has a great chance to put Chelsea in front from inside the Tottenham penalty area but Kinsky makes the save. It would have been a touch soft to give a free-kick to Tottenham but in the Premier League you suspect Tonali would have been awarded a free-kick there.

Tottenham are going to make a change at the back in light of Danso’s red card. Hardy is going to come on for Gallagher, who is booed by some of the Chelsea fans inside Accor Stadium. The England Under-18 international Hardy has come on at right centre-back in place of Danso.

Chelsea hit the frame of the goal. Pedro cuts it back from the byline to the penalty spot. Estevao gets to it first and his shot takes a deflection off Robertson. Kinsky makes a brilliant reflex save to push it onto the bar before Colwill blazes over.

Roberto de Zerbi is slumped in his seat distinctly unimpressed, shaking his head in frustration and perhaps disgust.

Palmer takes the free-kick but his effort is always curling wide of the far post.

The Austrian defender came on at half-time but has lasted just three minutes before being given his marching orders. Danso makes an absolute mess of a pass back to him from Gray and lets the ball run past him. Pedro gets around him and looks destined to drive towards the Tottenham penalty area but is brought down. Danso is shown a red card as Davies was probably not going to get across in time and it was the denial of a goal-scoring opportunity. Why do that in a pre-season friendly? Stupid.

Tottenham are making two changes at the break as Richarlison and Danso come on for Solanke and Van Hecke. Chelsea have also made a substitution as 16-year-old Nicoll-Jazuli comes on.

It appears the more times you see the incident involving Wesley Fofana and Conor Gallagher right at the end of the first half the more it looks like a penalty. Fofana did not appear to get the ball and instead catches Gallagher so Tottenham can probably feel a little aggrieved not to be given a penalty.

What have you made of that first half? Remember you can share your thoughts and opinions in the comments section at the bottom of the blog.

Possession: Chelsea 31%-69% TottenhamShots: 3-3Shots on target: 1-2Corners: 0-1

The first half is brought to an end and it is level at 1-1 at the break in Sydney.

Should Tottenham have been awarded a penalty? Robertson whips the ball in from the left to pick out the run of Gallagher into the box. Gallagher appeared to get to the ball ahead of Fofana, who seemingly then took Gallagher out but the referee does not point to the spot. That was a risky challenge to say the least from Fofana and on first viewing probably should have result in a penalty.

Palmer plays the ball forward to pick out the run in behind of Pedro, who has a two-on-one with Kinsky but the offside flag quickly goes up. Pedro was miles offside.

That was a decent opportunity for Tottenham. Tel finds the underlapping Davies with a pass towards the byline and the latter plays it across the six-yard box but Solanke was not there to meet it. Had Solanke read that, it would have been a simple tap-in.

Tel comes close to putting Tottenham back in front. It would have been a great solo goal as he drives inside from the left wing and moves into the Chelsea penalty area. He gets the better of Essugo on the corner of the six-yard box but is denied by a decent save from Sharman-Lowe.

Pedro has a chance to put Chelsea in front but his effort goes wide. Chelsea steal possession inside the Tottenham half after a poor pass from Robertson and the ball is then played forward to Pedro, who shoots from just inside the Tottenham box but his effort goes wide of the far post. Davies did just enough to put Pedro off.

Tottenham have two penalty appeals in quick succession turned down. First was for a potential handball by Essugo and then a push by Palestra on Tel. The handball would have been very harsh and the second incident was never a foul on Tel, who was losing his balance anyway.

Chelsea gift possession away deep inside their own half and Tel’s eyes light up. The ball rolls across to the Frenchman in a central position just outside the box and he opens up his body, trying to curl one into the top corner, but gets his first-time effort all wrong and his shot misses the target by a mile.

Like London buses, two goals come in quick succession and Chelsea are back on level terms. Chelsea counter from deep inside their own half and the ball ends up with Gittens on the left. From the corner of the box, he crosses towards the far post. It takes a touch off a Tottenham defender and ends up at the back post where Estevao, one of the smallest men on the pitch, beats Robertson and heads into the opposite corner.

Tottenham take the lead in Sydney courtesy of £100m signing Tonali. Solomon lays it back to Tonali who, from just outside the box, hits it first time and his shot takes a big deflection off Colwill, taking it into the far corner and giving Sharman-Lowe in the Chelsea goal no chance. That was probably Tottenham’s first proper foray forward in the game.

It has been a pretty stop-start game as play continues to be halted by fouls. The two managers might enjoy seeing the passion of their teams but they will also want to see their sides actually play, which is quite difficult when fouls are being committed left, right and centre.

Van Hecke has already fouled his former teammate Pedro once and he bundles into him again. Van Hecke has a wry smile as he walks away and Pedro tells the referee that is now twice he has been fouled by Van Hecke. I think it is a fairly safe assumption that Van Hecke and Pedro do not like each other that much!

We are not even 10 minutes into this friendly but there is absolutely no love lost between these two sides and the challenges are flying in. Former Chelsea man Gallagher slides in on Essugo, which infuriates the Chelsea players. The referee takes his time to make his decision as both sides come to blows before giving out the first booking of the game to Gallagher.

Pedro is caught by Van Hecke out on Chelsea left and the latter is absolutely furious with that decision, believing he got the ball. However, replays show that he did not get the ball and a free-kick was the right decision. Those two were teammates at Brighton and supposedly were involved in a training ground altercation just over a year ago!

The free-kick is whipped in towards the back post and the last touch is deemed to have come off Chelsea, much to their chagrin.

Lavia catches Tonali late and eventually the referee blows his whistle to bring play back for the free-kick. In a Premier League game, that may well have been a booking for Lavia. It might be a pre-season game but there will be no love lost between these bitter rivals.

The pitch in Sydney is on the bobbly side, which will make slick passing more challenging, dare I say it probably not really possible or realistic.

Both sides emerge from the tunnel, with Tottenham led out by Archie Gray and Chelsea by Levi Colwill. There is a lights show inside Accor Stadium as the teams making their way onto the pitch.

“My summer was great. I had seven weeks off or something, which I’ve never really had. I went on holiday with my family and I feel fresh. I didn’t know where to go. I went on holiday and I was thinking ‘where do I go next?’ I kept checking when I was back in. To be fair, I got bored in the sixth week. I was sat in Marbella thinking ‘I want to go back’ and I’ve never thought that!

“The first few months of me being injured, I just wanted to go out and play, which I probably shouldn’t have done as I couldn’t play how I wanted to play. I went to Sweden or Denmark to see a doctor and we did speak about surgery, but I didn’t end up getting it. It was a bad season, personally, with injuries and stuff, but I feel good now. Seven weeks off obviously helps, but I’m ready to go again.”

Mykhailo Mudryk, the Chelsea winger, has been cleared to return to competitive football with immediate effect after the anti-doping case against him was resolved.

Mudryk has not played for Chelsea since November 2024 after he tested positive for meldonium, a banned substance.

The Ukrainian has consistently insisted that he never knowingly used the substance and that he did not understand how it had entered his system.

#1930. Why Unai Emery is right to turn down Manchester United and stick with Aston Villa

It’s a great quirk of Premier League scheduling that Manchester United welcome Aston Villa to Old Trafford this weekend, after a week in which Jamie Carragher’s suggestion that Villa manager Unai Emery would jump at the chance to move to United prompted a legal threat from the midlands club, an apology from the outspoken pundit and an announcement late on Wednesday that Emery and his bosses had ‘positive discussions establishing a clear commitment beyond 2029 for the joint development of the club’.

A new contract is reportedly imminent for the Spaniard, and who could possibly blame Emery for sticking around at a club that have repeatedly backed him, given him more control than he’ll have anywhere else and whose fans worship him for delivering their first trophy in 30 years last season.

The alternative? Joining a constant catastrophe that everyone agrees needs far more than just a new manager to put back together.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

While Emery is going nowhere, the whole affair does raise questions about football’s food chain, something which definitely does exist but is clearly going through some changes right now.

Managers will always believe they are the right person to take a once great club and bring back the glory days, and being the one to do so is an intoxicating idea.

But Emery has been here before and was burned by his experience at Arsenal where a collection of expensive failed transfers and unmotivated senior players gave him the worst possible platform to build from. Sound familiar?

All roads still lead to Real Madrid for players but the money involved in Premier League football means simply being a relatively successful English club puts you closer to the top of the chain than ever before, and given United’s penchant for finding new lows every season, a move from Villa north to Manchester is at best a sideways move these days – just ask Youri Tielemans.

Also, given the relative state of flux that many of the ‘big six’ find themselves in these days, there’s an opportunity for Emery and Villa to elbow their way in and become a more established fixture towards the top of the league.

Select your team for football news tailored to you Close

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

United are joined by Spurs in their ability to self-implode, Chelsea are chaotic at the best of times, Liverpool are still just about managing the transition to a Jurgen Klopp-less existence and Manchester City are unlikely to be challenging for titles in the near future, depending on impending sanctions.

Only Arsenal are properly set up for consistent success, and Villa clearly believe trusting in Emery is the best way to eventually get themselves into the title conversation.

There are pitfalls to their approach – if Emery does someday get his head turned by a massive paycheck in Saudi Arabia or Real Madrid do come calling, he may still move on and leave the club as a ship without a sail, which is why clubs like Brighton and Brentford treat their managers as cogs in a well-oiled system.

United fans had some temporary relief midweek with their emotional comeback against Roma in the Champions League and may well go into the international break feeling good if they manage to squeeze out a win on Sunday, but regardless of the result, Emery is in the right place.

#1929. Chicago Fire vs Columbus Crew - prediction, team news, lineups

By Byron David | 05 Nov 2026 12:43, Last updated: 05 Nov 2026 20:40

Decision Day in MLS sees Chicago Fire searching for home advantage in the Best-of-Three series when they host Columbus Crew at Soldier Field on Saturday, November 7.

The visitors have every incentive to win the final regular-season match, as it would help them avoid the single-elimination wild card match.

Chicago have already done better than their regular-season performance from last term, as they cannot finish below fifth, which is three spots better than 2025.

The Fire will hope to go a step further, though, after the Philadelphia Union bundled them out in the Best-of-Three series last season.

Home advantage will be crucial for them going forward, but they must make it count on the final day to secure Soldier Field as the destination for the next phase of the playoffs.

Gregg Berhalter's charges are now unbeaten across their last three MLS fixtures, but they have not won any of their previous two games that they have hosted.

The Fire won the corresponding fixture last season, and avoided defeat in the reverse match earlier this term, but the visitors have a better head-to-head record.

Nonetheless, the hosts must win here to control their own destiny, as even a draw may not be enough for them to secure home advantage in the next round.

Alternatively, Chicago fans can quietly get behind Inter Miami, who will be entertaining Charlotte at the same time, as if the Herons win or draw with the Crown, then the Fire will be comfortably through to the next round, with the first game set to be at Soldier Field.

Columbus Crew have qualified for the playoffs in some form, but as things stand, they must contest the one-off elimination match.

Laurent Courtois will hope that his men can make a play for a Best-of-Three series spot with a win in Illinois.

The Black and Gold have won their last five MLS matches in a row, which means they will head into this fixture full of confidence.

The fact that they won three of the last four head-to-head matches in Chicago will further inspire them to cause an upset this weekend.

The visitors will secretly hope for Nashville to beat or draw with FC Cincinnati, which will open their path to the next phase of the competition.

It is mostly good news for the hosts as they head into the most important part of the MLS season, with South African defender Mbekezeli Mbokazi returning from injury.

Robert Lewandowski snapped an eight-game goal drought last weekend, when he came off the bench to hand his team the lead in their 4-2 win away to Colorado Rapids.

The Polish international then turned creator for Puso Dithejane to add some glitter to the scoreline, but he will certainly be important for Berhalter's men.

Another man that the home side will depend on is Ivorian Jonathan Bamba, who scored a brace last week, taking his goal contributions this season to 12.

The Fire will be without Robin Lod and Sam Rogers, who are both injured.

The Crew are sweating over the fitness of Brais Mendez, who has been excellent since joining as a Designated Player from Real Sociedad.

Wessam Abou Ali and Rudy Camacho are definitely out of contention for the trip to Chicago.

Dylan Chambost will be crucial for the visitors' creativity, as he has done recently for the Crew.

Brady; Dean, Elliott, Mbokazi, Allen; Saletros, D'Avilla, Haile-Selassie; Zinckernagel, Bamba, Gomez

Shulte; Farsi, Moreira, Zawadzki, Amundsen; Zarourv, Chambost, Bangoura, Habroune; Tapia, Rodriguez

#1927. Arsenal urged to avoid £64m transfer mistake after Micah Richards claim

Arsenal should be wary of selling Viktor Gyokeres in the January transfer window, according to former Gunners striker Jeremie Aliadiere.

Gyokeres produced his best performance of the season in midweek with a goal and an assist to help the Gunners beat Slavia Prague 2-1 in the Champions League.

But it has otherwise proved to be a frustrating few months for the Swede, who has started just one Premier League match for Mikel Arteta’s side so far this season.

Gyokeres amassed a respectable 21 goals in all competitions in his maiden season after arriving from Sporting CP for £64million, but now faces an uncertain future at the Emirates having fallen beneath Kai Havertz in the pecking order.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

With speculation likely to mount ahead of the January window, some pundits, including Micah Richards, have suggested that the Gunners should look to move Gyokeres on.

But former Arsenal striker Aliadiere believes that might be a mistake and ultimately leave Arteta short of options at the top of the pitch.

‘I think it’s all depending on the finances how much they can get for him and who to replace him with,’ Aliadiere told Metro.

‘Because I think as much as obviously he’s not in the top 11 now because Havertz is preferred number one, you don’t want to sell him, get a good price and not be able to replace him.

‘If Havertz gets injured, which obviously we’ve seen in the past – he’s had a few injuries and he can pick up injuries – you just end up with no striker at all.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘So I think it’s a very difficult January transfer window. Do you try to buy someone before you sell? I think when you look over the summer, selling Trossard and Martinelli before buying somebody.

‘Obviously, they go to Tzolis, but I’m not sure Tzolis was bought to be the first choice and when he is injured, you end up doing Eze on the left-hand side, and that’s not really his best position in my opinion.

‘So I don’t want it to happen with Gyokeres, thinking let’s try to sell him and recuperate a good transfer fee for him and then not replacing him.’

But even if Gyokeres remains at the club, Aliadiere can’t envisage the 28-year-old becoming the long-term solution to Arsenal’s search for a clinical striker.

‘I just feel the way Arsenal plays does not quite suit Gyokeres’ style of play,’ Aliadiere, speaking via football betting, added.

‘I’ve always been very quite patient and looking at the good stuff that he does, and I still feel that he does some amazing work. But I just do feel that the players don’t really give him the ball quick enough, which is what he needs.

‘He needs to be on 1v1. He needs to run the channel, get fed the ball quite quickly. And I feel we’re not really playing that way. We like to control the ball.

‘We like to control the tempo and just slow down the game. And I just feel Gyokeres is more of a counter-attacking player where he sees the space, he wants it quickly and then he’s on 1v1 and then he can then dominate physically.

‘But he’s rarely getting in that position, so I just find it difficult to kind of see him turning things around in a way of probably just being a rotation player.’

#1925. First Anfield victory for 14 years was vindication for Mikel Arteta after Fleetwood humbling. His Arsenal look the finished article - Liverpool were authors of their own downfall, writes OLIVER HOLT

Published: 13:54 EDT, 1 November 2026 | Updated: 06:32 EDT, 2 November 2026

Five nights ago, 40 miles to the north of Anfield at a remote outpost of English football, Arsenal fell to one of the most humiliating reverses of their long and august history. In the teeth of a gale that blew in off the Irish Sea, they were knocked out of the League Cup by Fleetwood Town, a team 18th in League Two.

They left with their tails between their legs, their teenage prodigy Max Dowman sent off in a melee, their heart questioned, their quality debated, their discipline an issue. Mikel Arteta and his side knew that just a few days later, at the other end of the Fylde Coast and across the Ribble Estuary, they would have to swap running the gauntlet of the Cod Army for the challenge of facing down the roar of the Kop.

They did not shirk it. If Tuesday night was a humbling, their gritty 1-0 victory in an Anfield that was a cauldron once more felt like a significant triumph. It was a defensive masterclass from the champions, an exercise in indomitability. It was their first victory here since 2012 and it took them above Manchester City so that they sit, once more, at the top of the table. Liverpool could not summon a single shot on target.

‘It felt like the end of the world when we were knocked out at Fleetwood,’ Arteta said after this win. ‘You look so silly. I was thinking “How can I lift these players up?” You have to dig deep. This was a mission to win here and it is something that we have not done for 14 years for a variety of reasons. We knew we would have to navigate some difficult moments.’

If Arteta left Fleetwood answering questions about his management of Dowman, he finished this game by striding on to the pitch after the final whistle, pumping his fists in front of the Arsenal fans celebrating in the Anfield Road end, and beating his hand on his chest. This was a vindication for him and his team. Five nights is a long time in football.

He had talked about the harsh realities of this sport after Tuesday’s loss. He had reminded everyone that playing at this level was not like ‘Disneyland’. And this victory was not like Disneyland, either. It was less a theme park and more an assault course. It was rough and it was unforgiving and Arsenal were equal to it.

Liverpool, improving under the management of Andoni Iraola, had been talked up as title contenders ahead of this match on a dank evening on Merseyside where the streets around the ground were decorated with the toothless grimaces of rotting pumpkins on doorsteps. The home team showed exhilarating signs of their re-emergence as an attacking force.

They dominated much of the game, too, but they looked like an emerging team, a team that is still evolving. Arsenal, marshalled imperiously by Declan Rice, looked like the finished article. They created one outstanding chance and Kai Havertz converted it. That was all they needed.

Their defence stayed rock-solid, although there was some puzzlement that Liverpool were not awarded a penalty for Jurrien Timber’s blatant shirt-pull on Alexander Isak. After the interval, Liverpool rarely looked like drawing level.

Kai Havertz gave the Gunners a lead to defend after finishing off a well worked move early on

The German slotted home after Declan Rice fizzed a dangerous ball across the six-yard box

Winning at Anfield was vindication for Mikel Arteta after Arsenal's defeat by Fleetwood Town

The opening had been predictably frenetic. Neither team forged a chance but Trey Nyoni, who has forced his way into the first team with a series of excellent performances in midfield, could have been booked twice inside the first quarter of an hour.

The initial infringement was a nasty tackle on Martin Odegaard inside the first minute where he planted his studs in Odegaard’s ankle. The second was a spiteful tackle on Kai Havertz. Neither received a yellow card, which gave yet more pause for thought about the red card shown to Dowman at Fleetwood, and its aftermath.

Let’s get one thing straight – the criticism of Arteta for his ‘treatment’ of Dowman was absurd. It has come to something when a manager giving a player a hard stare is interpreted by some as a disproportionate response.

Nobody is necessarily hankering after a return to the days of Sir Alex Ferguson’s hairdrier or Joe Kinnear’s rants that broke records for expletives but if a boss is attracting censure because he looked at a player a bit funny, we are in big trouble.

Arteta is not there to indulge Dowman. He is there to coach him and to teach him and to help him grow up in the context of a Premier League football club. His actions in Fleetwood on Tuesday fulfilled his obligations in all of those criteria.

Arsenal survived the initial frenzy here and took the lead after 16 minutes. Liverpool were the authors of their own downfall. They gave the ball away from a goal kick, it was worked to Noni Madueke on the right, and when Madueke fed it to Declan Rice on the overlap, Rice crossed beautifully for Havertz, who touched it home at the back post.

Arsenal nearly returned the favour a minute later when they played themselves into trouble at the back. Bradley Barcola found himself through on David Raya but his first touch let him down and Rice moved across to clear the danger.

Alexis Mac Allister was left with his head in his hands after missing a glorious chance to score

Liverpool's 19-year-old talent Trey Nyoni started the match but was replaced in the second half

Liverpool recovered and began to dominate the game. Barcola’s pace began to cause Arsenal all sorts of problems down their right flank and Liverpool came close to an equaliser when Virgil van Dijk flicked on a corner and Alexander Isak was denied by the brave intervention of Raya.

Arsenal were still threatening on the counter. Christos Tzolis chipped a ball to the back post and, as Liverpool scrambled to clear it, Madueke turned it back across goal. The ball was intended for Havertz, who was unmarked in the middle, but Timber could not get out of the way of it and it bounced off him into touch.

The atmosphere was febrile. Liverpool had three appeals for penalties, first for Timber’s shirt pull on Isak, then for challenges on Alexis Mac Allister and Cody Gakpo, turned down in quick succession. Tempers began to flare on the benches.

The breathlessness of the match was relentless. Florian Wirtz drove a free kick against the face of the crossbar with Raya beaten and then, three minutes before the interval, Mac Allister ran on to a cross from Milos Kerkez and, with the goal at his mercy, directed his free header too high.

Liverpool laid siege to the Arsenal goal after the break but the openings just would not come. Isak blazed high over the bar from an angle, Wirtz had a shot on the turn blocked and then, just before the hour, Dominik Szoboszlai replaced Nyoni and, to more acclaim, Rio Ngumoha came on for Gakpo.

Still Liverpool could not prise Arsenal open. Arsenal began to grow in confidence and threat. The home team were grateful to Jeremy Jacquet for a clearance that prevented Odegaard turning Tzolis’s cross into an open goal, for Van Dijk’s brilliant interception to deny Havertz and, most of all, for a quite magnificent one-handed save from Alisson that diverted a Tzolis shot round the post. It will stand the test of time as one of the saves of the season.

Arsenal put in another excellent defensive display to frustrate and keep Liverpool at bay

Liverpool’s frustration boiled over. Mac Allister was booked for his part in an ugly fracas with Odegaard and Madueke. The stands became a mass of pointing fingers and shouts of protest and anger. Time-wasting and play-acting peppered the match. Liverpool felt the game slipping away in the angst.

Liverpool threw everything at it in the final minutes. Lewis Koumas flung himself at a bouncing ball but could not get enough power on his header, Ngumoha had a shot charged down, Barcola desperately searched for pockets of space but could not find them. There were six minutes of time added on but there was no way through. Arsenal’s defence would not yield.

#1924. Thomas Tuchel reveals why Cole Palmer has been left out of England squad AGAIN

Thomas Tuchel has explained Cole Palmer is still paying the price for missing too many England camps after the Chelsea star was once again left out of his Three Lions squad.

Palmer was left out of the World Cup squad in the summer and withdrew from the group for the extended international break in September and October due to injury.

Tuchel warned it was a ‘missed opportunity’ for Palmer at the time, insisting he ‘misses way too many camps’ with other players moving ahead of him in the pecking order as a result.

Palmer has played almost every minute of Chelsea’s Premier League campaign this term with his injury problems from last season seemingly behind him.

But Tuchel made the decision on Friday to leave him out of the squad for upcoming Nations League games against Croatia and Spain with Jobe Bellingham and Fulham’s Josh King named ahead of him.

Speaking on Friday, Tuchel explained King’s versatility was a key reason for his inclusion ahead of Palmer. Morgan Rogers and Morgan Gibbs-White also also vying for the no10 spot with Tuchel explaining the group that impressed him training last month keep their places on merit.

‘It is enough no10s [in the squad] and we stick with guys who were in camp because camp was excellent for the two-and-a-half weeks we had together,’ Tuchel said.

Goalkeepers: Jordan Pickford (Everton), James Trafford (Leeds United), Jason Steele (Brighton)

‘The impact of other players was immense and that’s why we stick with the group and all the offensive players. We have Josh King in there but I also want to see him on both wings, he can play all four positions, that is basically the reason.’

Tuchel added: ‘Everyone is desperate to play for England and Cole is no exception.

By Ben Knapton | 05 Nov 2026 12:47

A spot in the UEFA Nations League knockout stages is on the line for England when they complete their League A campaign against Spain and Croatia during the November international break.

The Three Lions just need one point from their final two games to progress to the quarter-finals, and here, Sports Mole gives you the chance to pick your England squad for the November international break - be sure to download and share with your friends!

Tuchel should have no major quandaries on the goalkeeping front, as James Trafford and Jordan Pickford are shoo-ins, while Dean Henderson is likely to displace Brighton & Hove Albion veteran Jason Steele after recovering from injury.

However, the England boss now faces the age-old Ben White dilemma in defence, as the Arsenal right-back has stayed injury-free in recent weeks and has enjoyed a strong start to the campaign with the Premier League champions.

White has provided three assists in 12 games for the Gunners while starting seven of their nine top-flight fixtures, but he has not been selected for England since March; a hamstring injury ruled him out of the extended September/October period.

Tuchel must also weigh up whether to recall Harry Maguire, who has been a stalwart in an under-performing Manchester United side, and Djed Spence, who has forced his way into the Inter Milan XI after recovering from injury.

The biggest dilemma for the former Chelsea head coach undoubtedly comes in the final third of the field, though, as all eyes will be on whether Blues playmaker Cole Palmer is included in Tuchel's ranks.

Palmer pulled out of the September/October squad through injury, triggering a frustrated response from Tuchel, who admitted that the 24-year-old misses too many camps and his England future is potentially in jeopardy under the current regime.

However, a fully-fit Palmer could be offered a route back into the squad due to Bukayo Saka's injury, as the Arsenal winger is expected to be out until December with the quadriceps problem he sustained against Bayern Munich in the Champions League.

Noni Madueke and Phil Foden will also be fighting for attacking recalls, although the latter - who was also snubbed from the World Cup group - has already suggested that the November squad may come a little too soon for him.

Madueke, on the other hand, may be directly competing with Arsenal teammate Eberechi Eze, who was included in the September/October selection despite his fringe status at the Emirates.

Meanwhile, Dominic Calvert-Lewin was summoned to play second fiddle to Harry Kane last month, but having scored just once in his last five Premier League games, the Leeds United striker's spot could come under threat from Ollie Watkins.

Northampton have failed to get past the first round of the competition for the last six years and Chris Hogg's side head into Saturday's tie off the back of a 1-0 defeat to Oldham Athletic on Tuesday.

#1919. How Amorim engineered a derby masterclass: Tactical analysis of AC Milan 3-1 Inter

AC Milan tasted derby delight for the fourth time in a row as they dismantled Inter in the first half to take the bragging rights.

It did not take long for Milan to go ahead as Christian Pulisic rose highest to nod in a Diego Moreira cross, and just a few minutes later Adrien Rabiot was on hand to finish off a nicely worked set-piece routine to make it 2-0.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Alessandro Bastoni scored from a corner to make it a one-goal game once again, but then Moreira’s free-kick re-established the two-goal lead and that would be enough to see the Rossoneri home after a more controlled secnd half.

It marked a fourth straight win for Milan against the Nerazzurri and it reduces the gap to the city rivals back down to four points. Below is the tactical breakdown from Rohit Rajeev.

Ruben Amorim chose to make six changes from the team that lost to Bologna on Wednesday night, with Mario Gila, Sankhoun Diawara, Luka Modric, Adrien Rabiot, Diego Moreira and Christian Pulisic all getting the nod.

Milan started with a 4-4-1-1 formation, with Gila, Moreira and Rabiot returning to the starting XI. However, the structure was far from rigid, frequently shifting between a 4-2-3-1 and a 3-4-2-1. Much of this positional fluidity was dictated by the movements of two players in particular: Diawara and Rabiot.

Milan adopted a 3-4-2-1 structure in possession, using a one-up, one-down mechanism to maintain balance in their build-up.

When both Gila and Diawara pushed forward, Modrić dropped into the defensive line to preserve a back three. This ensured Milan always had three players providing rest defence and protection against counter-attacks.

This was one of the key differences between Amorim and Xabi Alonso’s approach at Chelsea. Alonso was more comfortable leaving just two players at the back, allowing Acheampong to advance and accepting the increased risk of counter-attacks.

Chivu was without his captain and leading goalscorer Lautaro Martínez, while also having one eye on Tuesday’s fixture against Feyenoord. He therefore experimented with a 3-4-2-1 formation, a system that had brought him success during his time at Parma.

Sucic and Diouf operated behind Thuram, with Barella and Çalhanoğlu forming the double pivot. However, the experiment backfired. Inter’s usual 3-5-2 offered greater central presence and allowed them to create numerical overloads, particularly when Lautaro dropped deeper to link play.

Without that additional central presence, Inter struggled to establish the same midfield superiority.

Amorim’s subtle shift from a 3-4-2-1 to a 4-4-1-1 was primarily intended to increase Milan’s presence in the wide areas.

With Inter heavily reliant on the flanks to progress their build-up, Milan used this adjustment to create numerical superiority, often establishing 4v3 situations in wide areas.

This allowed them to outnumber Inter around the ball, restrict their passing options and prevent progression. An effective example of horizontal pressing.

Much has been said about the build-up to Milan’s first goal, particularly the excellent combination play that allowed them to progress from the back and find Moreira. However, what followed was equally important.

A 2v2 situation developed in the wide areas, with Rabiot occupying Bastoni and Moreira taking on Carlos Augusto. Moreira won his individual duel, creating the opportunity to deliver into the box.

While this was unfolding, Milan committed three players into the penalty area: Ramos, Pulisic and Diawara. Pulisic’s movement was particularly intelligent. He initially checked his run, distracting Bisseck, who was more focused on the ball than tracking his opponent.

As the cross arrived, Pulisic moved into the space created by that moment of hesitation, set himself and finished clinically. A goal built on excellent individual quality and intelligent off-ball movement.

A rare set-piece goal for Milan, but one that involved the collective effort of several players. Milan used their players effectively as blockers, almost like in volleyball.

Ramos blocked Sucic, while Pavlovic and De Winter occupied Bisseck and Akanji. Diawara also engaged two Inter players, creating a completely free route between Moreira and Rabiot.

With Inter defending zonally, these blocking movements disrupted their defensive structure and left Rabiot unmarked. On cue, Rabiot attacked the space and met Moreira’s delivery to score.

A well-rehearsed set-piece routine built on intelligent movement and effective blocking.

Milan then moved to a 5-2-3 shape to defend the obvious attack from Inter who looked to recover in the game.

With Milan maintaining a high defensive line, Inter looked to exploit Thuram’s pace by playing chipped through balls into the space behind the defence.

After going 2-0 up, Milan took a significant defensive risk with their approach. The front three of Rabiot, Pulisic and Ramos continued to press high, while the back five held their position.

This created a considerable gap between the two units, which Inter were able to exploit during their counter-attacks.

Inter used rotations in the build-up to create numerical advantages in the wide areas. Barella dropped into the back three, allowing Bisseck to push forward and join Diouf and Spence on the right. This created a 3v2 against Diawara and Pavlovic, with Diawara particularly exposed to a 2v1.

The Nerazzurri replicated the same movement on the opposite flank, with Bastoni advancing and allowing Carlos Augusto to push higher up the pitch. This created the space for Augusto to deliver the cross that led to Djed Spence’s chance.

Inter scored their only goal from a corner. Calhanoglu delivered an inswinging cross, with Akanji making a decoy run towards the near post and flicking the ball on with his head. This movement attracted Milan’s defenders towards the front post, leaving Bastoni unmarked at the far post to head home.

Musah did well to position himself between the ball and Barella, winning a free kick in a dangerous area. Maignan also positioned two Milan players between Inter’s wall and Josep Martinez, obstructing the goalkeeper’s line of sight.

Moreira struck underneath the ball with the upper part of his instep, generating enough lift to send it over the wall and make it 3-1.

With Milan comfortably ahead, Amorim’s priority was to manage the game, and he did so effectively. He dropped the defensive line by around four metres and encouraged Milan to circulate possession more in their own half, avoiding unnecessary risks while Inter were forced to chase the game.

Milan also played more long balls in the second half, reflecting their increased willingness to exploit the spaces left behind by Inter through counter-attacks.

Inter were initially outnumbering Milan in central areas, but Amorim addressed the issue with a tactical adjustment. He instructed Pulisic and Rabiot to drop deeper, forming a midfield triangle that provided additional central support and prevented Inter from creating the same numerical overloads.

Amorim also introduced adjustments to neutralise the wide overloads created by Bisseck and Bastoni. He repositioned Pulisic deeper, asking him to track Bisseck’s movements and prioritise defensive duties over attacking influence. Pulisic therefore operated more like a midfielder than a traditional number 10.

Musah was given a floating role in front of the defence, acting as a screen and covering the spaces left behind whenever Milan’s defenders stepped out to engage an opponent or pushed forward to support an attack.

#1918. Malaga vs Racing de Santander - prediction, team news, lineups

By Matt Law | 05 Nov 2026 12:55, Last updated: 05 Nov 2026 12:57

Malaga's search for their first victory of the 2026-27 La Liga campaign will continue on Saturday afternoon when they welcome Racing de Santander to Estadio La Rosaleda.

The hosts will enter the match off the back of a 2-1 defeat to Real Betis, while Racing suffered a 3-0 home loss to Real Madrid last time out.

Malaga boast a record of five draws and six defeats from their 11 matches in Spain's top flight this season, with five points leaving them at the bottom of the La Liga table.

The White and Sky Blues did record a 3-0 victory over Alcazar in the Copa del Rey on October 27, but they were unable to back that up, losing 2-1 against Real Betis in their last league fixture.

Juan Francisco Funes' side are already five points from the safety of 17th spot and will certainly be wary of that gap widening ahead of the November international break.

Malaga have faced Racing on 30 previous occasions in all competitions and lead the head-to-head, having posted 13 victories to the latter's nine.

That said, Malaga are winless in their last six matches against Racing, with their last success in this fixture coming back in February 2020 in the Segunda Division.

Racing picked up a point on their last visit to Malaga - in last season's Segunda Division campaign - while they have been victorious in three of the last five games between the two sides, which is a record that will hand them confidence.

The Green and Whites were beaten 3-0 by Real Madrid last time out, with the result leaving them 16th in the La Liga table, picking up 11 points from 11 matches courtesy of a record of three wins, two draws and six defeats.

Jose Alberto's team actually have the worst defensive record in Spain's top flight this season, conceding 29 times in their 11 games, which is eight more than Malaga.

That said, Racing have been relatively strong down the other end, scoring 15 goals, while Malaga have only found the back of the net on eight occasions.

These are the type of matches that could have a big say in determining whether Malaga, Racing or both teams are capable of avoiding relegation this season.

Racing de Santander form (all competitions):

Malaga can certainly take plenty of positives from their performance against Real Betis last time out, so it would not be a surprise to see the same XI take to the field.

Adrian Nino has scored five times in seven league appearances for Malaga this season and will once again feature in the final third of the field for the hosts.

However, all of Juan Cruz, Angel Recio, Diego Murillo, Pablo Martinez, Joaquin Munoz, Julen Lopete and Aaron Ochoa are set to miss the match due to fitness issues.

As for Racing, Jorge Salinas will make a welcome return to the squad, having served his suspension against Real Madrid last time out.

However, Andres Martin is once again expected to miss out with a muscular issue; Alvaro Mantilla is also set to be absent with the injury that forced him off early against Real Madrid.

Yassir Zabiri has scored eight times in 11 league appearances this season, and the 21-year-old will continue in the final third of the field.

#1917. Gabriel and Mac Allister's cheating is not just embarrassing, it's malevolent and wicked... players need the threat of red cards for such dishonesty and - if that fails - punishments after review, writes IAN LADYMAN

Published: 18:05 EDT, 1 November 2026 | Updated: 06:37 EDT, 2 November 2026

Football’s lawmakers like to meddle. The problem is they do it in areas that tend not to need any meddling. Like around handball and offside and other places that were doing just fine as they were.

So here’s a tip for the meddlers at the International Football Association Board. Meddle somewhere that needs it. Meddle in a way that would be meaningful and important and in a way that would actually help the game.

Please meddle with cheating. Please do something that would spare us from the embarrassment of grown men behaving like children in a bid to get other players booked and sent off. Yes, please meddle there.

Because football at the top level really needs it.

It needs a route through which players such as Alexis Mac Allister and Gabriel Magalhaes can be properly punished, shamed and embarrassed for what they did during Sunday’s otherwise fabulous Premier League game between Liverpool and Arsenal at Anfield.

It needs a deterrent. It needs greater power to match referees and greater leeway for retrospective punishment.

Alexis Mac Allister drops to the floor holding his face after his forehead is slightly brushed

The Liverpool man tried to get Noni Madueke sent off during Arsenal's 1-0 victory at Anfield

In a way, it is handy that there was one from each team this time. That way, we can be spared the usual accusations of bias that tend to come when footballers are called out for their sins.

Here, live on TV, Gabriel and Mac Allister were both as bad as each other. One in each half, clear as day.

Arsenal defender Gabriel was poked in the chest early on by Aleksandar Isak and went down holding his face. Then, much later, Liverpool’s Mac Allister was brushed by the forehead of Noni Madueke and did likewise.

Neither fooled referee Andy Madley. Both were told to get up and get on with the game. On TV, Sky Sports analysts Gary Neville and Jamie Carragher didn’t hold back.

‘Embarrassing’ was the word they both chose. Neville to describe Gabriel and Carragher as a way of calling out Mac Allister.

But this type of chicanery is more than that. We see it from lots of players and we see it all the time. It’s not just embarrassing. It goes much deeper. It’s malevolent. It’s low. It’s pre-meditated. It’s wicked.

Short of dark subjects such as spitting and leg-breaking tackles, I can’t think of much worse things on a football field than pretending to have a head or facial injury when you actually haven’t.

So where IFAB need to get involved – where they need to ‘meddle’ – is simple. They must increase football’s powers to punish.

On the field and in the moment, referees can issue yellow cards for simulation and for cheating. Players can be booked for exaggerating contact (Mac Allister) or pretending contact has been made with a certain area of the body when it hasn’t (Gabriel).

Arsenal defender Gabriel Magalhaes performed a similar act of cheating in the first half

The Brazilian fell down clutching his face after Alexander Isak brushed his neck and chest

But why is there no power – at least in occasional and exceptional circumstances - to issue a red card?

Gabriel and Mac Allister appeared to be trying to get their opponents sent off. Would they do it if they knew the match referee at least had the option of showing them the red card instead?

Retrospectively, meanwhile, we need greater leeway for action.

Under a law passed a decade ago, a player can theoretically be banned by a review panel for two-games for ‘successful deception of a match official’. However the reality is that the initiative has largely been superseded by VAR and was only really used for players diving to try and win penalties anyway.

In terms of the nonsense we witnessed at Anfield on Sunday – and indeed see on a reasonably regular basis around the country – there is very little recourse once the game is over so once again a possible deterrent has been removed from the equation.

Cheating of this nature currently looks and feels like a risk worth taking and that is what must change.

Alexander Isak was not given a penalty despite being blatantly pulled back by Jurrien Timber

Here, it was interesting to hear Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola suggest afterwards that he must start telling his players to go down under contact. He was talking about Isak’s refusal to buckle under a clear penalty area shirt tug from Jurrien Timber.

That’s an important issue, too. Players should not be punished for their honesty. A foul is a foul, regardless of the reaction. VAR should have awarded a penalty.

But here on an otherwise fine day for the Premier League, another known and rather ugly blot on the landscape grew larger.

The threat of red cards for cheating and – if that fails - punishments handed down by review. That’s the kind of meddling we should all be on board with.

#1916. GdS: Amorim ‘changes the pieces’ – his plan to rotate vs. Ferencvaros in must-win game

AC Milan don’t have much time to enjoy their derby win over Inter, as a key European game awaits on Thursday night.

La Gazzetta dello Sport (seen below) begin a report this morning by writing that this week marks the beginning of a genuine push toward success in the Europa League. The momentum gained from the derby victory must be harnessed and used properly.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

For a Milan side capable of dismantling Chivu’s team with three goals in 45 minutes, the Ferencváros game should pose no real concern. It must, however, be approached with focus and a significant yet carefully considered rotation of the squad.

The situation mirrors the league campaign in one key respect: the table. By winning on Saturday, Milan got back into the hunt for the Scudetto, so a similar result is needed in Europe. The Rossoneri currently sit on three points, while the Hungarians have a perfect record of nine.

Even with a win, Milan won’t catch their opponents, but they will improve their position in the table which is a necessity, especially with only four games left after this.

Ferencvaros’ position in the standings is the result of a long, arduous journey. They began their Europa League campaign in the first qualifying round, eliminating Serbia’s Vojvodina.

In the second round, they knocked out the Dutch side Twente. They then triumphed over Poland’s Górnik Zabrze in the third round, before defeating Trabzonspor in the play-offs.

All that hard work has paid off in the league phase, where they have secured three wins out of three – against Celtic, Plzeň and Torreense – making them one of only five teams with a perfect record. The others are Benfica, Leverkusen, Bournemouth and Olympiacos.

Two of these four have already faced the Rossoneri, which speaks to the challenging nature of Milan’s schedule. Against the Portuguese side, Amorim faltered in his debut, fielding a side packed with reserves in a high-profile match.

Against Bournemouth, the result was compromised by two penalties and Mike Maignan’s red card. In between, there was a resounding victory in Salzburg, spearheaded by Alphadjo Cissé. This explains why they currently sit on just three points, a situation that now demands a turnaround.

The upcoming schedule is relatively more manageable, featuring an away trip to Athens, a home match against Sunderland, a visit to Sofia to face Levski, and a game against Ararat Armenia in Milan.

Securing a spot in the round of 16 is a task that needs to be completed, and preferably soon. Sitting on three points in 24th place, Milan’s current standing in the Europa League does not reflect the goal the club have set for themselves: to go all the way in the competition.

Cisse will return to the starting line-up for the competition in which he is the team’s top scorer: three goals, all netted on the same night in Austria. The squad will once again be adjusted to accommodate the turnover and rotations necessary for managing resources.

This time, the team are better prepared to absorb these changes after welcoming back some players before the derby. Consequently, there will be further rotation on Thursday night, with the aim of keeping everyone fresh.

A change is unavoidable in goal, where the suspension for the captain Maignan will see Lorenzo Torriani make his first start. In defence, Sankhoun Diawara could play centrally, while Pervis Estupinan or Davide Bartesaghi (or both, with the latter pushed further forward) could feature on the left.

In midfield, Ardon Jashari will take on a Modrić-like role, while the versatile Filippo Terracciano could slot in as a mezzala (or even at right-back, covering for Mario Gila). There is also a chance of seeing the very young Christian Comotto in action.

In attack, Omari Hutchinson is a certain starter:he looked lively during his time on the pitch against Bologna and performed even better against Udinese, a match in which he scored his first goal for Milan. Cisse could lead the line, but Francesco Camarda and Goncalo Ramos remain candidates too.

#1915. Bradford City vs Marine AFC - prediction, team news, lineups

By Calum Burrowes | 05 Nov 2026 13:10, Last updated: 05 Nov 2026 13:18

Aiming to cause a major FA Cup upset this weekend, Marine AFC travel from Merseyside to Yorkshire to face League One side Bradford City on Saturday afternoon.

The Bantams head into the cup tie without a league win in their last few outings and on the back of a weekend defeat to local rivals Huddersfield Town, while the Mariners are also winless in three matches and have slipped to 18th in the National League North table.

Bradford City will be looking to reach the second round of the FA Cup for the first time in two years when they welcome opponents from three divisions below them.

The Bantams, now led by Michael Duff following Graham Alexander's departure to Preston North End, have enjoyed some memorable cup runs over the past decade, with their journey to the quarter-finals in the 2014-15 season a notable highlight.

In January 2015, Bradford travelled to Stamford Bridge to face Jose Mourinho's Chelsea, producing one of the biggest upsets in FA Cup history as they came from two goals down after 38 minutes to secure a remarkable 4-2 victory over a side competing in the Champions League at the same time.

At the time, Chelsea were top of the Premier League while Bradford were sixth in League One, leaving 49 places between them, 20 fewer than the gap separating the Bantams from their upcoming opponents.

More recently, Bradford are still in League One, although just one win in their last five league matches has seen them slip out of the playoff places and down to seventh, seven points behind the division's leaders.

As for Marine, they make the trip to Valley Parade without a win in their last three matches, having followed a draw against Oxford City with defeats to Chester and Buxton in the National League North.

Indeed, Bobby Grant's side last tasted victory in the FA Cup, when a 2-0 win over Hartlepool United secured their place in the first round proper.

Like their upcoming opponents, the Mariners have enjoyed a famous FA Cup occasion of their own, with their 2021 meeting with Tottenham Hotspur at Rossett Park remaining a standout moment in the club's history.

The third-round tie, also against a Mourinho side, took place during the height of the COVID-19 pandemic and ended in a 5-0 victory for Spurs, with Carlos Vinicius scoring a 13-minute hat-trick.

The 161-place gap between the clubs was the largest in FA Cup history, while the sale of 32,202 "virtual tickets" raised more than £300,000 for Marine.

Since that memorable occasion, the Mariners have spent three consecutive campaigns in the National League North, where they have won just five of their opening 14 matches this season and sit 18th, only one point clear of the relegation zone.

Duff was always likely to make changes for a cup tie against opposition three divisions below Bradford, but injuries sustained in the defeat to Huddersfield could limit his options.

Adam Phillips was introduced at half-time in that match but was forced off four minutes from full-time after picking up an injury, making him unlikely to feature on Saturday.

Phillips will join Stephen Humphrys and Josh Neufville in the treatment room.

Captain Antoni Sarcevic was sent off during the Yorkshire derby last weekend, but he is available for the cup tie as his suspension only applies to league fixtures.

As for the visitors, Grant could name the same starting XI that lost 4-2 to Buxton on Halloween.

Goalkeeper Jack McIntyre has made 11 appearances this season and kept two clean sheets, and he is expected to start between the posts at Valley Parade.

Finlay Sinclair-Smith has provided four assists and scored twice in the National League North this season, and he could feature in attack alongside Charlie Jolley.

Dawson; Pennington, Baldwin, Pratt; O'Keeffe, Sarcevic, Pointon, Touray; Powell, Beesley, Swan

McIntyre; Drysdale, Butler, Wardle, Whittingham; Raikhy, Whelan, Darby; Sinclair-Smith, Jolley, Simms

With 69 league places currently separating the sides, Bradford are clear favourites to progress and should have too much quality for their non-league visitors.

Marine will hope to make life difficult for the hosts, but we expect the Bantams to take control and secure a comfortable victory.
