#1888. How Alvaro Arbeloa sparked Fulham revival to save his job

Ex-Real Madrid boss had looked on the brink at Craven Cottage before timely resurgence, with work still to do

When Alvaro Arbeloa was reminded of Fulham’s torrid record at Villa Park, a little smile broke out across his face.

He knew his team, in drawing 1-1 with Unai Emery’s side, had shown further evidence they are on the right track and turning around a season that had started woefully.

Arbeloa was not a universally popular appointment at Craven Cottage and this time last month was a pretty good bet to become the first Premier League manager sacked this season.

The narrative has changed now. As one fan said, “from being one game from the sack to earning seven points from three games is a brilliant return”.

How much credit Arbeloa personally deserves for Fulham’s turnaround is up for debate, but that moment when the ex-Real Madrid manager imminently faced the chop never materialised.

Last month, when Fulham had lost to strugglers Sunderland, Crystal Palace and Ipswich, and still had zero league wins, the club’s owner Shahid Khan appeared to come out in support of Arbeloa ahead of the home game against Hull.

“We have been in every match, missing only the opportunities we've had to complete the task,” Khan said. “I believe those opportunities will soon be seized - especially if we have our supporters in full voice today and beyond.”

Fulham were 1-0 winners over Hull in a game where plenty of fans believed they were deserving of a more emphatic scoreline to match their dominance.

Another clean sheet followed - in a 1-0 win at Coventry - before that draw against a Villa team who were then second only to holders Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League table.

“We have proved that we can compete with anyone,” said Arbeloa.

And Fulham had needed to get to that point under the Spaniard, not only because Premier League survival will depend on it but also because that was precisely what Marco Silva’s team did so well across four seasons in the top-flight.

A little sprinkling of luck is always needed when rectifying a bad situation, and Villa goalkeeper Zion Suzuki dropping a corner over the goal line did feel like the fortunate moment in question at a club where the players, manager and backroom staff had all been feeling hopelessly down on their luck.

Arbeloa is known to still be annoyed by Fulham’s wastefulness in front of goal; they are the third-biggest underperformers in the league for xG. Missed chances has been the one binding thread throughout his time in charge.

We have proved that we can compete with anyone

New striker Gonzalo Garcia has had his fair share of woes in that area and patience is beginning to wear thin from a fanbase not known for knee-jerk reactions.

When the defeats were piling up, Arbeloa reminding people of his stature within the game was an ugly look. Ex-Real Madrid manager or not, he needed to deliver deeds, not words. Fulham have begun to.

Where he deserves credit is in adapting his system. “At least he is prepared to change his ideology,” Fulham’s record goalscorer Gordon Davies tells Standard Sport, “because we’ve had managers in the past who are only prepared to play Plan A.”

The high-intensity pressing Arbeloa insisted upon in those opening games was wholly at odds with how Silva’s Fulham had played and the squad looked unable to bridge the gap between what they knew and what the new manager wanted.

“It worried supporters, especially given that you have a new manager, new players, and in the first game of the new season give a goal away after 30 seconds,” Davies recalls.

Arbeloa softened, becoming more pragmatic and accepting that results and only results would save his job as he headed for the brink.

A kind run of fixtures did eventually get Fulham out of their hole, though the Cottagers’ distinct lack of a clinical edge remains a major problem and a potential obstacle to them realising their potential.

Because their underlying data is impressive. In the ‘expected Premier League table’, Opta’s model says Fulham, who in reality are 15th, ought to be eighth.

Fulham are more possession-based under their new manager, their attacking patterns more zippy and lively than at the end of Silva’s tenure, when some felt they were “stale”.

Silva was exceptional at judging which substitution to make and when, though - the area representing Arbeloa’s greatest shortcoming so far.

Centre-backs Calvin Bassey and David Affengruber have been among Arbeloa’s trustiest performers, while 19-year-old midfielder Josh King has come on immensely.

Statistically his displays this season are night and day compared with last term, and he is shouldering real responsibility for his age.

While they may face difficulty trying to keep hold of him in the long-term, he has no shortage of fondness for the club that made him, telling Standard Sport in an interview in April: “My personal ambitions will come - but I feel I do have a certain loyalty to Fulham.”

Hosting Newcastle on Saturday is huge: a winnable game before a fairly long run of tricky fixtures. The pressure eased, Fulham must now kick on.

#1886. St Mirren vs Rangers - prediction, team news, lineups

By Ellis Stevens | 05 Nov 2026 15:01

St Mirren welcome high-flying Rangers to the Marbill Coaches Stadium on Saturday for a matchday 13 clash in the Scottish Premiership.

The hosts are eighth in the table with 14 points from 12 games, while the visitors are second with 24 points from 11 matches.

St Mirren enjoyed a fantastic start to the Scottish Premiership season, winning three and drawing one of their opening four games, including keeping three clean sheets and scoring seven goals in that time.

However, the Saints' fortunes quickly took a turn for the worse after a 2-1 defeat to Celtic in early October, with St Mirren subsequently embarking on a five-game losing run.

St Mirren did end that run with a 2-1 win against Dundee, followed by a 1-1 draw with Hibernian, but they were handed their sixth league defeat in 12 matches against Motherwell last time out, losing 1-0 to a late Lukas Fadinger penalty.

The Saints have, as a result of their recent run, slipped to eighth in the standings with 12 points from 12 games, while only Kilmarnock (28) have conceded more than their 20 league goals this term - a far cry from the impressive start to the season that saw them keep three clean sheets in four matches.

Goals have also been hard to come by during that time, scoring only five goals in their last eight matches, although they have managed to find the net three times in their last two matches at the Marbill Coaches Stadium.

Craig McLeish's side have actually been at their best at home throughout the season, winning two, drawing two and losing two of their six home league fixtures, including remaining unbeaten in their last two home games, and they will be relying on that strength when they take on Rangers on Saturday.

The Gers head into matchday 13 as the Scottish Premiership's most in-form team, having remained undefeated in their last nine league games, recording seven victories and only two draws during that time.

Rangers, who have also booked their place in the Scottish League Cup final with wins against Celtic (3-0) and Aberdeen (1-0) during that run, have climbed to second in the league table as a result of their superb run.

Derek McInnes, who actually failed to win any of his first four matches as Rangers manager, will be looking for his team to continue that stunning run and pick up another three points on Saturday, especially as they trail leaders Celtic by just four points - while also holding a game in hand over their Old Firm rivals.

Rangers are the only team still yet to taste defeat away from home in the Scottish Premiership this season, recording three wins and three draws on the road, and they also won 1-0 in their last visit to St Mirren's home ground.

The Gers have also demonstrated their dominance in this fixture twice already this season, recording a crushing 5-1 triumph over St Mirren in the Scottish League Cup second round before winning 1-0 in the league in early September.

St Mirren are contending with at least five injury absences, including Ismael Kabia, Keanu Baccus, Malik Dijksteel, Nikolas Agrafiotis and Jonah Ayunga.

Following an underwhelming offensive performance in the loss to Motherwell last time out, McLeish could look to make changes on Saturday, meaning the likes of Chris Mochrie and Jake Young could start.

Rangers are also dealing with numerous injury issues, with Cameron Devlin, Daisuke Yokota, Jose Cifuentes, Lawrence Shankland, Ross McCrorie and Youssef Chermiti all unavailable.

Ryan Don Naderi scored the winner against Aberdeen in the Scottish League Cup semi-final on October 31 and is also Rangers' top scorer in the league with five goals, and the forward should start just behind Kevin Kelsy on Saturday.

#1885. Crystal Palace 1-1 Hoffenheim: Daichi Kamada on target in stoppage time to ease pressure on Pierre Sage

Daichi Kamada’s last-gasp leveller salvaged a 1-1 Europa League draw for Crystal Palace against Hoffenheim after Adam Wharton was sent off in the second half at Selhurst Park.

Alexander Prass opened the scoring when his effort squeezed under Dean Henderson in the seventh minute of the contest, and Palace could not find a reply.

Wharton was dismissed in the 77th minute in south London, 19 minutes after he was first booked following an aerial challenge.

Just as it looked like the already under-pressure Pierre Sage was heading for another defeat, Kamada found the back of the net in second-half stoppage time.

Kamada had the ball in the back of the net in the fourth minute, the end of a set-piece sequence, but the offside flag was raised.

The Germans then made it a nightmare start for the hosts, who did not react quickly enough on a counter-attack and allowed the visitors to work the ball to Tim Lemperle, who delivered a lovely cross to Prass.

His low shot initially looked straightforward enough for Henderson, but the Palace captain could not contain his initial stop and the ball trickled with an agonising inevitability towards, then across, the line.

Hoffenheim remained in the driver’s seat, and there were numerous chances for the visitors to pad their lead – Fisnik Asllani fizzed a shot wide, threatening enough to draw a dive from Henderson, who later saved a second effort from the Kosovo international, then one from Andrej Kramaric.

Palace finally enjoyed a sustained spell of attack around the half hour. Kamada flashed an effort across the face of goal, just wide, and Jean-Philippe Mateta first tried to nod home, then called Oliver Baumann into a rare stop.

Palace were giving the ball away too easily as the second half got under way, and they were lucky to avoid conceding for a second time when Kramaric was released but curled wide of the left upright.

Sage made a double-change five minutes before the hour, swapping Quinten Timber and Anan Khalaili for Eddie Nketiah and Oscar Mingueza.

Several Palace players, including a bewildered Wharton, vehemently protested, but the referee was unmoved and the hosts were reduced to 10.

Sources in Germany are confirming that Markus Krösche should be announced by AC Milan in the coming weeks, ready to start in January.

It is seemingly not a very well-kept secret by this point that Milan are looking to appoint Krösche as their new Head of Football, having made an attempt to get him in the summer. Sources in Italy have claimed things are done, but their German colleagues have always been a bit more hesitant.

Meanwhile, Eintracht Frankfurt have already settled the question of Krösche’s successor. Joti Chatzialexiou is coming from 1. FC Nürnberg and will take over the position of sporting director. So, it seems like just a matter of time.

#1882. Max Dowman continues Premier League ban amid new Arsenal suspension risk for Hull clash

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta is still at risk of a suspension, despite avoiding a yellow card in the win over Liverpool.

As Arsenal cruised to a 2-0 win over Everton last month, the second half booking for Arteta could prove costly at some point this season.

The Gunners boss was cautioned by referee Tony Harrington, seemingly for leaving his technical area at the Emirates Stadium and means it the Spaniard has been booked twice in nine Premier League matches.

The first yellow card came against Sunderland in September, also for leaving his technical area, as he fumed at some of the refereeing decisions despite Arsenal emerging victorious at the Stadium of Light.

As a result, Arteta must watch his step on Saturday when the Gunners face Hull in the final match before the November international break.

A booking at Emirates Stadium would move Arteta onto three yellow cards - which for managers guarantees a one-match suspension - so the Gunners boss would have to serve a touchline ban against Newcastle on November 21.

Just like the rules for players, there is a cut-off point regarding bookings for managers. Therefore, Arteta is at risk of a suspension for three bookings right up until the 32nd Premier League fixture of the season.

Reacting to his second yellow card of the domestic season, Arteta insisted there are other managers far more culpable than he is.

"I do have to be careful,” Arteta said in the post-Everton press conference. “I’m going to put sensors there. There are managers that have the record in the league, 36 times in 10 minutes leaving the touchline, no yellows.

“So I'm clipping all of that. I have a massive storage of images. So if somebody is going to say [anything], I'm not the record yet, somebody else has the record.

"Then it's 36 yellow cards in 10 minutes for the manager. I don't know where we're going to be."

Arsenal have already been dealt one suspension blow this season after losing an appeal to have Max Dowman’s red card against Fleetwood overturned.

#1881. Michael Carrick hits back at suspicions that he is on the brink of the sack at Man United - and insists he is relishing Tuesday's battle against Roma

Published: 10:06 EDT, 2 November 2026 | Updated: 10:07 EDT, 2 November 2026

Michael Carrick doesn’t feel like he is on his last legs as Manchester United head coach – but admits people might think he is ‘crazy’ for looking forward to the Champions League clash with Roma at Old Trafford on Tuesday night.

Speaking ahead of the game at Carrington on Monday, Carrick also insisted that he has no concerns over Lisandro Martinez’s commitment despite the Argentine’s reckless red card at Chelsea on Saturday.

United go into the game against Roma in danger of equalling a club record of ten consecutive games without a win in a single season set by Dave Sexton’s team in March 1978.

Last week, United bosses gave Carrick more time to turn the season, but there is a growing suspicion that he could be sacked in the international break after the next two games against Roma and Aston Villa.

Asked if he has the same feeling, Carrick said: ‘No, not at all. Listen. I can’t look into the future, and you never know what's going to happen. I don't know what's going to happen.

‘That doesn't change the way I feel. That doesn't change how we're preparing for the game tomorrow, and I'm actually really looking forward to the game. I can't wait for the game tomorrow.

Michael Carrick does not feel like he is on the brink of the sack at Manchester United

'You might think I'm crazy with the results we've had and what's going on, but I genuinely, really can't wait for the game tomorrow, and that's all I'm focused on, really I am.

‘Whatever happens, it is going to happen, but we want to make it a big night tomorrow night first.

‘It's what I am, it's what I live for, you know. A lot of people could do my job when you're winning a lot of football games. It's about finding the solutions, finding the answers, staying strong, leading right and getting the best out of the players.

‘We've got to keep pushing for that. But it doesn't change my mindset at all. I love being here, I love working with the players, and the struggles and the challenges, that just drives you on to want it even more.’

Martinez is available to face Roma but will be banned for the Villa game on Sunday after he was sent off for two bookings in the space of 82 seconds at Stamford Bridge – earning the second yellow card for striking Wesley Fofana in the face.

It followed the Argentine’s outburst against club bosses, and director of football Jason Wilcox in particular, after United were beaten by Atletico Madrid last month.

However, Carrick insisted there are no concerns over Martinez’s commitment or the general discipline in the dressing-room after Bruno Fernandes criticised his tactics in the defeat to Como a fortnight ago.

‘No, I've got no concerns about commitment at all,’ said Carrick. ‘Things happen in football. Sometimes you do things, sometimes you make a decision, sometimes you make mistakes, sometimes it goes well for you. But the commitment is not an issue for sure.

‘The dressing room is a good, good place, so perceptions are a funny thing. They can make things look all sorts of different ways and think about all sorts of different things. I've said it before, the commitment of the players to the club, to me, to each other, I don't question that at all. We need to play better, we can make better decisions, but commitment's not a thing at all.’

He says he is excited for Tuesday's Champions League clash against Roma - despite the potential for another embarrassment

Martinez and Fernandes are out of contract in June, although United have an option to extend both by 12 months. They are in talks with Fernandes but Martinez faces a more uncertain future at Old Trafford.

‘You know how discussions go and when anything's finalised, we'll let you know. But at this stage, there's nothing any further to update really,’ said Carrick.

Patrick Dorgu returned to training at Carrington on Monday after six weeks out of action but the Dane won’t be involved against Roma. Luke Shaw and Marcus Rashford missed the session and will remain on the sidelines with Benjamin Sesko and Manuel Ugarte.

United badly need a win after picking up three points from their first three games against Sabah, Atletico Madrid and Como. They sit 20th in the league phase. After Roma, they face Sporting Lisbon, RB Leipzig, Bayern Munich and Villarreal.

‘Of course we're looking for the win,’ said Carrick. ‘There is the bigger picture and it’s about getting through to the later stages. One or two games you can get away with really, as long as you make amends for that. Tomorrow and the games coming up are going to dictate that for us. So we're certainly still in it with a great chance of progressing, and it's got to be the focus for now.’

Roma’s only defeat in all competitions this season came in a dramatic 4-3 collapse to Real Madrid in the Champions League. But they have lost on all four of their visits to Old Trafford including a 7-1 defeat in 2007 – when Carrick scored twice – and 6-2 in 2021.

‘Long time ago, eh?’ smiled Carrick. ‘It was a magical night, I have to say. It was one of the best nights, one of the best games, one of the best atmospheres I've been fortunate enough to witness.

‘So the fact that I scored a couple and that was very unusual gives me great, great memories. But it was more the whole emotion of the night really. I have to say that it was a special one.’

#1880. Dowman weaves his magic and new signing shines as Arsenal hit ground running

Teenage sensation Max Dowman was the star of Arsenal’s first pre-season match, as he scored one goal and assisted another in a 4-1 victory over Girona.

Dowman, 16, was joined on the scoresheet by new signing Christos Tzolis, who struck with a low effort in his first game since his £34m move from Belgian side Club Brugge.

Established attackers Kai Havertz and Gabriel Jesus also scored for the Premier League champions, who were largely comfortable against opposition from the Spanish second tier.

Here are four things Telegraph Sport learnt from the match:

It was this time last year that Dowman first announced his remarkable talent to the wider world. Then only 15, he sparkled in pre-season and made it clear to Mikel Arteta that he was ready to impact matches at the highest level.

A year on, Dowman is now an established first-team player. He is the youngest ever Premier League winner and the competition’s youngest ever scorer, and he looks set to make even more of a mark this season.

In this friendly against Girona, Dowman created Arsenal’s opening goal with a gorgeous defence-splitting pass for Havertz. He did so after receiving the ball under pressure and spinning into space. Dowman then scored Arsenal’s third with a powerful low drive from the edge of the box.

Dowman is in competition with Bukayo Saka and Noni Madueke for a place on the right wing, which means this summer represents a huge opportunity for the teenager. After playing for England at the World Cup, Saka and Madueke will both miss most of pre-season.

Dowman, therefore, has a serious chance of going into the new campaign as the starting right-winger. The Community Shield on August 16 must be a target in his mind.

“We know what he’s capable of doing,” Arteta said. “We want to be more consistent in terms of the performances and the actions that he can deliver, but I think today he had a really good game.”

Arsenal are close to completing a deal for Newcastle United captain Bruno Guimarães but, for now, their only outfield signing of the summer has been Tzolis. This was the Greek winger’s first match in front of supporters and he immediately demonstrated why Arsenal were willing to pay £34m to buy him from Club Brugge.

With Tzolis, it is all about the final product. Goals and assists. He struck 22 times for Club Brugge last season, and registered 29 assists.

How did he produce such impressive numbers? The answer could be seen in his first-half goal against Girona. Receiving the ball on the left wing, Tzolis quickly accelerated towards the penalty area and unleashed a low shot. It was perhaps a more direct approach than Arsenal would usually have seen from Leandro Trossard, the player Tzolis has replaced, and it caught Girona off-guard as the ball deflected into the net.

“I’m very pleased with him,” Arteta said. “First of all, the way he has adapted to the club, to the team. The connection he’s already generating with the boys. I think you’re going to love the player.

“A player who’s very direct. He’s got the goal between the eyes. He has a lot of similarities with Leo [Trossard] in a lot of the things that he can do and the spaces he can occupy. And then the work rate that he has... He’s a boy that comes with so much hunger. He wants to prove himself, it’s a dream for him. And we are here to help him.”

Havertz was one of the few Arsenal players who benefited from playing at the World Cup. His injury issues mean that, unlike most of his team-mates, he did not end the 2025-26 season in a state of exhaustion.

After returning to the pitch in the spring, Havertz enjoyed an impressive end to the campaign for Arsenal. He then performed well at the World Cup, scoring three goals for Germany.

He remains one of Arteta’s favourite players, not least because of his versatility. He started in attack in the crucial end-of-season games in May, but played in midfield against Girona. His low finish, from Dowman’s pass, represented his eighth goal in his last 12 matches for club and country.

Girona’s goal, scored by Arnau Martínez, was perhaps the only alarming moment of this comfortable pre-season victory. Martínez was unmarked from a left-wing corner when he powered a header into Arsenal’s net.

For a group of players who pride themselves on their set-piece prowess, this was a disappointing moment. It also perhaps showed Arsenal’s reliance on their two first-choice centre-backs, William Saliba and Gabriel Magalhães, when they are defending crosses into their box.

Gabriel arrived at Arsenal’s pre-season training camp a few days ago, so he should be in good shape by the start of the new campaign. Saliba, though, will be missing for months with a back problem.

Without Saliba’s height and power, will Arsenal be as effective from set-pieces in the opening chunk of the campaign? Coventry City, Arsenal’s opponents on the first night of the season, will undoubtedly look to test the champions in these situations.

The reigning Premier League champions are handed the Costa Brava Trophy, which is half-heartedly lifted into the air by White. There will be far bigger trophies on offer to Arsenal in the upcoming campaign.

Arsenal have cruised to a routine 4-1 win over Girona, with Havertz, Tzolis, Dowman and Gabriel Jesus all finding the net. Arteta will be delighted with his side’s professionalism and ruthlessness.

Meslier takes too long on his goal kick, gifting a corner to Girona. However, the delivery from the hosts is so poor as it flies harmlessly out of play. That sums up Girona’s difficult evening.

There is another round of substitutions for both sides.

Once again, Meslier makes a pivotal stop on his Arsenal debut. Martin clips an exquisite pass over Arsenal’s defence to the onrushing Ruiz, who is through on goal. The striker takes the chance first time, but Meslier is there to make another crucial save.

Arsenal’s makeshift line-up, which is full of Hale End graduates, is holding firm, with Girona evidently struggling for attacking inspiration. If Arsenal can see out this victory without any injuries, then it would have panned out exactly how Arteta would have wanted.

Girona carelessly give possession away in defence, allowing Nelson to dribble towards the penalty area. The winger floats a cross into the box, which is met by O’Neill, but the forward’s lofted header hits the top of the bar.

There is cooling break in this second half to give both sets of players a quick breather. It’s been a professional performance from Arsenal, who now have various academy prospects on the pitch. Can any of them follow in Dowman’s footsteps and make an eye-catching impression in this match?

Girona make another flurry of changes, giving the youngsters from the club’s academy an opportunity to impress.

Dowman was the breakout star of pre-season last year, when he was only 15, and he has started this campaign in similarly thrilling fashion. One assist, one goal. As you would expect, he looks bigger and stronger.

Arsenal overturn the ball in midfield and it breaks perfectly into the Brazilian’s path. Gabriel Jesus is one-on-one and makes no mistake, applying a devastating finish to make it 4-1 and put the result beyond any doubt.

The 16-year-old prodigy now has a goal and an assist. Dowman picks up the ball in the right attacking pocket, palms off Moreno, who bizarrely throws himself to the ground holding his face, before firing a resounding effort into the bottom corner. He’s such a talented footballer and looks at home in Arsenal’s first team.

Out of nothing, Girona have pulled a goal back. Kim whips a corner into the box, with the unmarked Martinez slamming a magnificent header into the top corner, leaving Kepa rooted to the spot. Arteta will be furious with his side’s complacency there.

The good news for Arsenal is that Gabriel is back with the squad and should be ready to go for the start of the campaign. The bad news is that Saliba’s back injury will rule him out for months. Will that lead to more sustained vulnerability over the opening chunk of the season?

Girona have sent a host of players out to warm up. They’re playing in their fourth pre-season match, with their league campaign due to start on August 16 against Leganes.

We are back under way for the second half.

That was a straightforward half for Arsenal. Arteta will be pleased with Havertz’s showing in his 33 minutes on the pitch. After missing so much of last season through injury, it has been a good summer for Havertz so far. He scored three goals in Arsenal’s final six games of 2025/26, and then netted four times for Germany in June.

The 2009-born playmaker was Arsenal’s standout player in that first half. Dowman’s confidence and class on the ball has been brilliant, with his expertly-crafted assist for Havertz’s opener an obvious highlight.

Dowman dribbles into the penalty area with ease, drifting past a couple of defenders before he is apprehended by Moreno. He goes down, but there is very little in the challenge.

Arsenal are in cruise control here. Girona are chasing shadows. Unsurprisingly, there’s a real gulf in class and quality between the two sides.

Once again, Dowman dances away from Moreno. The youngster sets up White with a reverse pass, but the Arsenal captain’s disappointing cross drifts out for a goal kick.

Tzolis registered 22 goals and 29 assists for Club Brugge last season. He is an end-product machine, and that goal was a little indication of how he racks up such eye-watering numbers. After receiving possession on the left wing, he was so quick to shift the ball onto his right foot and fire the shot at goal. He describes himself as a “direct” player and that was evidence of it.

There are three early changes for Arsenal, with Gyokeres, Havertz and Hincapie taken off for Gabriel Jesus, Vieira and Salmon.

The new winger is one-on-one with Martinez and darts inside, before firing a low effort into the bottom corner. It took a slight deflection, leaving Gazzaniga with no chance. Tzolis has looked lively and slotted into Arsenal’s attack seamlessly so far.

Tzolis is slipped into the penalty area from his left-wing berth, but instead of shooting, he tries to find Gyokeres with a pass. Girona surround the Swede before Dowman’s follow-up strike is blocked.

Since their goal, Arsenal have assumed real authority of this encounter and look like the far superior side.

Girona captain Martinez slams a powerful long-range effort at goal, but it fizzes wide of the bottom corner. Kepa seemed to have it covered regardless.

Arsenal are hunting for a second, with Lewis-Skelly picking out Havertz with a floated pass. The former Chelsea man is inches away from teeing up Gyokeres for a second, but Gazzaniga is there to make a goal-saving interception. Dowman has also been heavily involved in these early stages, providing the assist for Havertz’s opener.

After his extraordinary breakthrough campaign last year, Max Dowman has a huge opportunity this summer. With England wingers Bukayo Saka and Noni Madueke not returning until later in pre-season, Dowman has a chance to take ownership of the right wing position ahead of the Community Shield. His assist for Kai Havertz, a lovely measured pass after an excellent piece of skill in midfield, was a sign that Dowman means business.

Dowman drifts inside and pops up in the right channel, wriggling past Moreno, before threading a delightful pass through to Havertz. One-on-one, the German calmly slots a close-range effort into the bottom corner, giving Arsenal a well-deserved lead. So much credit must go to Dowman, who has started this game excellently.

Girona have some sustained possession to take the sting out of the game then burst into Arsenal’s penalty area, with the ball attempted to be pulled back to Van De Beek. The visitors have good numbers defending and comfortably deal with the danger.

Tzolis floats a free kick into the box, which Gyokeres meets at the back post. The striker directs the ball back across goal towards Calafiori, whose close-range header is caught by Gazzaniga.

It also appears that Havertz and Nwaneri have been tasked with quite free-roaming attacking midfield roles, with Lewis-Skelly positioned as a one-man holding pivot. It’s a strong but experimental line-up from Arteta.

After suffering an injury at the end of last season and missing the World Cup, White returns to action here this evening and wears the armband. He will look to support Dowman, who appears to be starting on the right wing.

It’s been a confident start from Arsenal, who are stroking the ball around in a very assured manner. Havertz looks to pull the strings by firing a low cross towards Gyokeres, but the delivery is scrambled clear by the Girona backline.

White leads Arsenal out onto the pitch to face Girona, who boast the likes of Van de Beek, Gil and Moreno in their starting XI.

Talking earlier this week, Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta sent out a determined message to other clubs by outlining their ambitious transfer plans.

“A lot is happening,” Arteta said. “We all know about the context of this transfer window. From ownership to the board, the sporting director and myself, we know that we want to take this club to a different level.

“That is going to require a better squad, better individuals. We have identified where we have opportunities to grow and to improve and to evolve our game and what is going to be needed to achieve that. Hopefully very soon we can start to put things in a very concrete way.”

Arteta also believes that last season’s Premier League title has served as added motivation for his squad to improve and hit new heights.

“This has to be the start and this has to be the standard,” he said. “Excellence has to be our standard and this has to drive to attack the future. The way we behave daily with more and more determination and ambition, because we’ve shown that we’ve got it. Now we have to show that we belong to this level and we want to increase and take this football club to a different dimension.”

It had been a relatively quiet transfer window for Arsenal, who have recruited just goalkeeper Illan Meslier and winger Christos Tzolis.

However, Arsenal are now moving very bullishly, closing on Newcastle United midfielder Bruno Guimarães, while also targeting Real Madrid’s Vinícius Júnior.

Sam Dean has the full breakdown of a potential deal for the Real Madrid star and how Arsenal are prepared to continue flexing their muscles in the transfer market in what would be one of the biggest moves in Premier League history.

It was January 2025, with Arsenal earning a hard-fought 2-1 comeback victory in the Champions League courtesy of first-half goals from Jorginho and Ethan Nwaneri.

Since this European encounter, Girona have been on a seriously downward trajectory, enduring lowly 16th and 19th finishes in La Liga, with the latter ensuring relegation to the Segunda Division, where they’ll play in the upcoming campaign.

August 12: Arsenal vs Como (London, England)

August 16: Arsenal vs Manchester City (Cardiff, Wales)

Mikel Arteta’s side will then begin their defence of the Premier League title on August 21 when they host newly-promoted Coventry City on August 21.

Arsenal are closing in on one of the statement signings of the summer, with Newcastle United midfielder Bruno Guimarães getting closer to joining the Premier League holders.

This deal means that Christian Norgaard is expected to leave and seal a move to Everton for around £7m.

As previously reported by Telegraph Sport, Guimarães has been Arsenal’s top target for weeks. It is believed that he will cost around £80m.

Hello and welcome to our live coverage for this pre-season friendly between Girona and Arsenal at Estadi Montilivi in Catalonia.

With the transfer speculation surrounding Vinícius Júnior’s and Bruno Guimaraes’ potential moves to Arsenal ramping up, the reigning Premier League champions are in action against Girona as they step up their preparations ahead of the upcoming campaign.

Unlike other Premier League heavyweights, Arsenal have kept their pre-season tour relatively local with a selection of games in Spain, Ireland and England, before they face Manchester City in the FA Community Shield on August 16 at the Millennium Stadium in Cardiff.

Arsenal beat League One side MK Dons 3-0 in a behind-closed-doors friendly on July 25 at the Sobha Realty Training Centre, thanks to goals from Reiss Nelson, Ethan Nwaneri and Ceadach O’Neill.

After featuring in this victory and setting up Nelson for the opener, Christos Tzolis will be looking to continue his positive momentum with his new club, after joining Arsenal for £34m earlier this summer. Many fans will be keeping a close eye on the recently-signed winger given that various core members of last season’s Premier League-winning squad are yet to return from their post-World Cup breaks, having progressed deep in the competition.

Tournament winners David Raya, Martin Zubimendi and Mikel Merino, Norway captain Martin Odegaard, as well as England internationals Bukayo Saka, Declan Rice, Eberechi Eze and Noni Madueke are all missing for this game, while France’s William Saliba is out injured and set for an extended period on the sidelines.

Those who exited the World Cup earlier than the aforementioned players, including Gabriel Magalhaes, Gabriel Martinelli, Piero Hincapie, Kai Havertz, and Viktor Gyokeres, have all joined up with the squad in northern Spain.

Mikel Arteta’s men will play a wounded Girona, who suffered relegation from the top flight of Spanish football last season due to a 19th-place finish.

Kick-off is at 19:00, with team news arriving shortly.

#1879. Daniel Farke confirms Leeds injury latest before Tottenham clash

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau

Leeds top scorer Dominic Calvert-Lewin is a doubt to face Tottenham this weekend after suffering an injury setback.

Calvert-Lewin, who has scored five goals across all competitions, has been an ever-present for Leeds in the Premier League so far this season, starting all nine games and completing 90 minutes in all but three appearances.

However, that record is under serious threat after Leeds boss Daniel Farke revealed the 29-year-old is dealing with a foot problem that forced him to miss training on Thursday.

“Dominic Calvert-Lewin had a little setback with his foot as well, was not able to train with us today but I would say I am carefully optimistic that he is back in training hopefully tomorrow and then he would also be available,” Farke said in his pre-match press conference.

Elsewhere for Leeds - who welcome a resurgent Tottenham to Elland Road for Saturday’s lunchtime kick-off - Joe Rodon could be available to face his former club, while Noah Okafor and Anton Stach are also doubts.

“Some mixed news during this week,” Farke added. “Good news with Joe Rodon, he is back in full team training during this week.

“Of course he was out for quite a time but it is definitely good because he is an important player for us and, yeah, back in training.

“In the offence we still are struggling a little bit. Noah Okafor obviously missed the last game due to some adductor problems.

“He was also not able to have one team training session during this week so far, just individual work for him. So, I can’t really say if he is available for the game.

“We have two more days anyhow but so far he has not joined us in team training.

“The same for Anton Stach with foot problems. Just individual rehab work was possible, so major doubts then both if they are available. With Anton and Noah we have to see.”

While the teenager marked the occasion with the opening goal of the game after just eight minutes, the Red Devils went on to crash out of the competition in the third round, meaning Lacey has had to remain patient for another start.

#1876. Torino vs Lecce - prediction, team news, lineups

By Jonathan O'Shea | 05 Nov 2026 15:12, Last updated: 05 Nov 2026 15:14

Both beaten again last week, Torino and Lecce will look to end their losing streaks when they meet each other on Saturday.

While Toro have just suffered back-to-back defeats, their visitors are also sliding down the Serie A standings.

After enduring a slow start to the season, Torino then posted their best run of league wins since 2019, but they have been unable to make such form last.

Having previously taken maximum points from three consecutive games, Toro then lost to two of Serie A's in-form clubs - Como and Frosinone.

First, Ignazio Abate's side conceded three late goals at home to Como, before Frosinone struck twice in the second half last weekend.

Only free-falling Udinese have shipped as many goals as Torino's nine during the final half-hour, which will cause Abate significant concern.

Furthermore, before returning to Turin, their last league clean sheet at Stadio Olimpico Grande dates all the way back to early March.

That said, the Granata have kept clean sheets on all of Lecce's last four visits, including a 1-0 win earlier this year.

Either home or away, Lecce have lost five of the last eight Serie A meetings, failing to even score in six.

Finding the net has been a familiar problem for several seasons, but the Salentini kicked off the current campaign relatively well, winning two of their first four league fixtures.

However, they have since lost four of the next five, including a 5-1 thrashing by Frosinone and last week's 2-1 home defeat to Genoa.

Perhaps not now, but in August that pair would have been considered Lecce's direct relegation rivals, making those losses sting even more.

In his second year at the southern club, head coach Eusebio Di Francesco surely faces another survival fight, as his team have now slipped down to 14th place.

Previously poor travellers, Lecce have actually won half of their last eight away games, so at least they can head north with some hope.

Torino will again be without Alessio Cacciamani, who recently dislocated his shoulder, but fellow wing-backs Niccolo Fortini and Ricardo Rodriguez might be involved this weekend.

Another wide man, Rafik Belghali should recover from a bruised knee, but midfield fulcrum Rolando Mandragora may be given the international break to fully overcome his thigh problem.

The matchwinner in this fixture last season, Che Adams is set to partner Giovanni Simeone up front; since his arrival in 2024, the Scotland striker is Toro's top Serie A scorer with 19 goals.

Highlighting their dearth of potent forwards, Lecce's last eight league goals have been scored by as many different players - including midfielder Youssef Maleh last week.

Willem Geubbels and Lassana Coulibaly will both be assessed before Saturday's game, but Joel Monteiro injured his left calf against Genoa; Medon Berisha, Santiago Pierotti and Ivan Ilic are still sidelined.

Bolstering his options at the back, Di Francesco can recall Kialonda Gaspar, who returns after serving a two-match suspension.

Perri; Coco, Ismajli, Comuzzo; Belghali, Gineitis, Braganca, Patterson; Vlasic; Adams, Simeone

Falcone; Veiga, Siebert, Gabriel, Gallo; Kaba, Ngom, Maleh; N'Dri, Stulic, Fatah

Although Torino have been leaking too many goals, they possess more attacking thrust than their limited visitors.

Since April, Lecce have gone 14 league games without a draw, and that streak will continue with their fourth straight defeat.

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

#1874. Blackburn Rovers vs West Ham United - prediction, team news, lineups

By Darren Plant | 05 Nov 2026 15:27, Last updated: 05 Nov 2026 15:28

West Ham United make the trip to Blackburn Rovers on Saturday afternoon looking to build on Wednesday's remarkable comeback against Cardiff City in Scott Parker's first match in charge.

At a time when the Hammers sit in eighth position in the Championship table, Blackburn are in 14th spot after consecutive defeats.

When West Ham were 3-0 down at Cardiff City on Wednesday night, Parker had the defence that he had only been in charge for less than a day.

Fast-forward to full time and the former Hammers midfielder had delivered a team talk that inspired his new set of players to a 3-3 draw against opponents who have not lost at the Cardiff City Stadium in seven Championship games.

Parker will have concerns over West Ham conceding three goals for the third match in succession, yet the potential of this team remains apparent when they have scored at least six more goals than every other club in the division.

With Middlesbrough losing to Wrexham, West Ham actually made ground on top spot, reducing the deficit to five points when not performing to their true ability.

Furthermore, it has gone under the radar that West Ham are yet to lose an away match this season, recording three wins and four draws from seven fixtures.

As far as Blackburn are concerned, they would have taken 14th place at this stage of the season had it been offered to them at the start of August.

However, Tony Mowbray's side have lost three of their last four Championship contests, albeit two of them coming at West Bromwich Albion and Swansea City.

Blackburn also went down 2-1 at home to fifth-placed Stoke City on Tuesday night, ending a run of three successive wins at Ewood Park.

Although Blackburn sit five points adrift of the playoffs, West Ham are in the final spot, so this contest has the potential to make-or-break their ambitions in the short term.

With Ryan Alebiosu an injury doubt, Gady Beyuku could be handed a start at right-back for Blackburn.

Moussa Baradji's goal as a substitute versus West Ham may also see him recalled in placed of Kristi Montgomery.

Unless Yuki Ohashi is brought back into the team, the rest of the side could stay the same.

Ezra Mayers, Mohamadou Kante and Joel Piroe are all in contention for West Ham, a consequence of their half-time introductions versus Cardiff helping spark the turnaround.

While the return of Tomas Soucek to the starting lineup is also a possibility, Parker may opt against further changes.

Blackburn Rovers possible starting lineup:

Toth; Beyuku, Carter McLoughlin, Pickering; Morsy, Baradji; Fevrier, Cantwell, Afolayan; Gudjohnsen

West Ham United possible starting lineup:

Hermansen; Veltman, Mavropanos, Kilman, Mayers; Bowen, Engels, Kante, Solomon; Mukasa; Piroe

While there is a vulnerability about West Ham that Blackburn will hope to exploit, the Hammers will be full of belief in the final third after Wednesday night. With that in mind, we expect their superior attacking quality to come to the fore to deliver a much-needed three points.

#1873. Transfer news LIVE: Arsenal eye triple deal; huge Man Utd manager twist; Chelsea, Liverpool, Tottenham latest

The January window is fast approaching as Arsenal, Chelsea, Manchester United, Liverpool and Tottenham all pursue some huge new mid-season signings to help reach their goals. Arsenal are said to be targeting a move for Antonio Nusa as they also eye Eli Junior Kroupi and Kenan Yildiz, with the likes of Alex Baena also believed to be in Mikel Arteta’s sights along with Julian Alvarez.

Didier Deschamps has reportedly turned down the chance to manage Manchester United, where Sunday’s game against Aston Villa will be crucial to determining the future of under-fire boss Michael Carrick. Tottenham are understood to still retain matching rights for Harry Kane after the England captain signed a record-breaking new Bayern Munich contract that is believed to make him the highest-paid player in Europe in terms of base salary.

Chelsea are confident of signing Alex Scott when the market reopens in the New Year, while Liverpool are keen on a swoop for Mexico wonderkid Gilberto Mora and Lamine Camara as Trent Alexander-Arnold continues to be linked with a sensational switch back to Anfield. Follow all the latest transfer news, rumours and gossip live below!

Didier Deschamps has reportedly turned down an approach over the Manchester United manager’s job, as more details emerge over the future of Michael Carrick.

Carrick’s position at Old Trafford has been subject to severe scrutiny for several weeks now following a miserable eight-game winless run across all competitions that was the club’s worst since the 1988/89 season.

Such a dire sequence was only snapped on Tuesday night as Man Utd staged an incredible turnaround following an abysmal first half to beat depleted Roma 3-2 at home in the Champions League, though it remains to be seen how much respite that offered their beleaguered head coach.

Sky Sports report that there remains support for Carrick within the United hierarchy, who have been said to be split on a potential replacement amid strong links to the likes of former Newcastle boss Eddie Howe and ex-Germany manager Julian Nagelsmann.

Real Madrid look to have won the race for Manchester United sensation JJ Gabriel.

The teenage star shocked Old Trafford chiefs back in September by stating his desire to leave the club immediately, just days before he was expected to make his senior debut aged just 15.

All of the rest of the heavyweight clubs across Europe were inevitably interested in signing one of the brightest youth talents in England, but Real Madrid and Barcelona quickly emerged as the front runners.

Madrid were said to be leading the race, with Fabrizio Romano now reporting that Gabriel has chosen the Bernabeu and that his camp have informed all parties of his decision.

The move is expected to be sealed soon, with Man Utd likely only due minimal training compensation.

Tottenham retain matching rights on Harry Kane despite his new Bayern Munich contract, reports claim.

The England captain yesterday put pen to paper on a lucrative contract extension in Bavaria until 2029 that is said to make him the highest-paid player in Europe in terms of base salary.

That bumper new deal does not impact Tottenham’s first-option right to match any future bids for Kane, per The Telegraph.

That agreement was reached during his initial exit from Spurs in 2023 and is said to lie outside of his contract, so has been unaffected.

Didier Deschamps has reportedly told Manchester United that he is not interested in taking over as manager at Old Trafford.

Michael Carrick’s future as Man Utd boss remains hugely uncertain ahead of Sunday’s crunch home Premier League clash with Aston Villa, which is likely to prove pivotal.

Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann had previously been considered as the leading candidates for the role if United - who will not consider an interim solution this time - were to sack Carrick, though FootMercato in France reported on Thursday that the club had also approached former long-time Les Bleus head coach Deschamps.

However, he is said to have told them that he currently has no interest in the job in another blow to the beleaguered Red Devils.

Arsenal are tracking Antonio Nusa ahead of the January transfer window, reports claim.

The Gunners are known to be keen on attacking reinforcements when the market reopens for business in the New Year and have reportedly had their eyes on Bournemouth forward Eli Junior Kroupi and Juventus winger Kenan Yildiz.

However, The Sun say that Arsenal are also keeping close tabs on former Club Brugge star Nusa, who continues to impress for both RB Leipzig and Norway.

Could a lucrative triple deal yet be in the offing at the Emirates Stadium after a somewhat disappointing summer?

Calciomercato claims that Juventus are considering a January move for Manchester United striker Benjamin Sesko despite his injury.

The Italian club have a €100million transfer budget following a capital injection and are assessing several attacking targets.

Folarin Balogun is also under consideration as Juventus explore options to strengthen their forward line.

Reports in Spain say that Barcelona have identified Arsenal defender Piero Hincapie as a potential signing for the January transfer window.

Sporting director Deco has made initial contact with the 24-year-old's representatives to explore a possible move.

Hincapie has struggled for regular minutes, but Mikel Arteta is reluctant to let players leave Arsenal in January.

Teamtalk claims that Manchester United have intensified their interest in Como defender Jacobo Ramon ahead of the 2027 transfer windows.

The 21-year-old is valued at around €50million, with Chelsea also keen and Arsenal, Liverpool and Fulham monitoring him.

Real Madrid hold a 50% sell-on clause and buy-back options, with a potential return to Spain under consideration.

Fichjaes claims that Barcelona have identified Manchester City left-back Rayan Ait-Nouri as a potential January signing.

The 25-year-old has made just three appearances this season, with City valuing him at around €30million.

Barca could pursue a deal if Alejandro Balde leaves, while Manchester United are also interested.

Unai Emery will not be going to Manchester United.

The former Arsenal and PSG boss is said to be a “dream target” for Old Trafford chiefs in the event that they sack Michael Carrick.

However, The Telegraph report that Emery is in advanced talks over signing a new long-term contract at Villa Park.

Villa said yesterday that Emery had been involved in an “important working meeting to plan the club's future and lay the foundations for its long-term sporting and institutional project”.

That meeting - in which they discussed committing to joint development beyond 2029 under Emery’s leadership - also involved chairman Nassef Sawiris, president of football operations Roberto Olabe and director of football operations Damian Vidagany.

#1871. Heartwarming moment Luis Suarez spots former Liverpool team-mate's son - now Chelsea academy starlet - and poses for a photo

Published: 08:34 EDT, 2 November 2026 | Updated: 10:14 EDT, 2 November 2026

Luis Suarez shared a heartwarming moment with former Liverpool team-mate Glen Johnson's son Kobi while at Inter Miami's training complex in Fort Lauderdale.

The 39-year-old Uruguayan was at the ground for the Messi Cup, a youth tournament the MLS side is hosting, and spotted Kobi Johnson lining up with the rest of the Chelsea Under-14s, who are competing in the United States.

The former Liverpool and Barcelona striker went over to the youngster and said: 'I used to play with your dad, I've known you since you were little.'

The one-time Champions League winner then smiled for a photograph with the youngster.

When asked about the chance encounter, teenage Johnson said: 'He (Suarez) just said like, he remembers when I was a little boy and I was quite chubby, and then he asked for a photo.'

Johnson has been at Chelsea from the under-eights and has risen through the ranks, steadily gaining a reputation as an exciting young talent.

Suarez shared a sweet moment with Glen Johnson's son Kobi at Inter Miami's training ground in the US

Kobi Johnson is currently on the books at Chelsea where he is tipped to follow his father into professional football

Suarez and Johnson spent four seasons together at Liverpool between 2011 and 2015

And it is clear to see where he gets it from, with his father Glen having played 357 Premier League games at Chelsea, Liverpool, Portsmouth and Stoke, even winning the league with Chelsea in 2005 and 2006.

It was at Liverpool, however, where the right-back played with Suarez for four seasons between 2011 and 2015 - with the pair were part of a memorable Liverpool team that narrowly missed out on the title back in 2014 after the famous 'Gerrard slip' at Stamford Bridge.

It was during that period too that Suarez was accused of racially abusing former Manchester United left-back Patrice Evra during a Premier League grudge match between the two clubs in 2011.

Suarez was subsequently banned for eight matches after it was ruled that he had used racist language towards Evra.

Johnson controversially publicly defended him at the time, and years later, continued to be conflicted over the incident.

Speaking on talkSPORT in 2019, Johnson said: 'Carra (former team-mate Jamie Carragher) was right to apologise and I'd have to agree with him; I think the timing of it was wrong as the ban was so close.

'But in the club's defence, they were just trying to support one of their players.

'I don't think anyone in that dressing room or at the club believed Luis was racist or capable of being racist.'

While 42-year-old Johnson is enjoying his retirement after leaving the professional game for good in 2018, Suarez is still plying his trade in America at Inter Miami alongside other Barcelona legends like Sergio Busquets and Lionel Messi.

#1870. Careless Liverpool concede same goal twice in second-half capitulation against Leeds

Leeds United came from 2-0 down at half-time to beat Liverpool 4-2 at Soldier Field in Chicago as Andoni Iraola’s side were undone by sloppy defending in the second period.

Liverpool’s dominant first-half display was underlined by goals from Luke Chambers and Florian Wirtz. However, Daniel Farke’s men replied with four strikes in 25 second-half minutes through Sean Longstaff, Brenden Aaronson and two alarmingly similar goals from Dominic Calvert-Lewin.

🎯 "CALVERT-LEWIN ARRIVES!" pic.twitter.com/CaHOeXQn7E

🤩 "Calvert-Lewin makes it FOUR!" pic.twitter.com/mEEi882OWi

Liverpool centre-back Chambers, 22, who spent last season on loan at Charlton Athletic, opened the scoring on seven minutes, pouncing on a Dominik Szoboszlai corner which had been flicked on at the near post by Milos Kerkez.

Jeremie Frimpong, serviced by a wonderfully flighted cross-field ball by Trey Nyoni, then set up Wirtz to make it 2-0 five minutes before the break, but on the hour Leeds began their recovery when Aaronson scored following a mistake by Kerkez – who gave up possession to Ethan Ampadu in his own half.

GOAL! Aaronson pulls one back! 2-1 pic.twitter.com/tdy17cITSd

Ampadu’s long throw was flicked on to Calvert-Lewin to level the score, then minutes later Curtis Jones’s carelessness allowed Longstaff in to put Leeds in front.

🔥 "LONGSTAFF! WHAT A TURNAROUND!" pic.twitter.com/G9LvLIk0Mi

And it was a familiar story five minutes from time when Ampadu’s throw again prompted chaos in Liverpool’s back line, allowing Calvert-Lewin to steal in front of Jones and seal victory.

Liverpool return to Anfield for friendlies against Monaco and Como before they begin their Premier League season away at Newcastle United later this month.

Leeds have matches against RB Leipzig, Manchester United and Augsburg before their league campaign gets under way at Nottingham Forest.

July 25- Leeds 2 Wrexham 3July 30- Leeds 1 Sunderland 0Today- Leeds 4 Liverpool 2August 8- Leeds vs RB LeipzigAugust 12- Leeds vs Manchester UnitedAugust 15- Leeds vs Augsburg

July 25- Liverpool 4 Sunderland 2July 30- Liverpool 1 Wrexham 0Today- Liverpool 2 Leeds 4August 9- Liverpool vs MonacoAugust 16- Liverpool vs Como x2

Possession: Liverpool 57%-43% LeedsShots: 9-15Shots on target: 3-7Corners: 3-7

The final whistle is blown in Chicago and that has well and truly been a game of two halves. At half-time, Liverpool were in complete control with a 2-0 lead. However, four Leeds goals in 25 second-half minutes have given Daniel Farke’s side the victory at Soldier Field. Both sides will now return home to the UK.

Aaronson is booked for a cynical pull on Ramsay.

Koumas should score for Liverpool. He is played in behind and for some strange reason Cairns comes a long way out of his goal. Koumas should lift it over Cairns and into the empty net but gets his chip wrong and the shot goes off target.

Leeds’ second half gets even better and Liverpool’s gets even worse. It is a very similar goal to Calvert-Lewin’s first; Ampadu’s long throw is flicked on and Calvert-Lewin meets it, heading past Mamardashvili. This is very much your game of two halves.

Daniel Farke is making a double change as Gnonto and Lienou come on.

Frimpong kicks the ball out of play and he may have a problem. Is it just cramp or more serious than that? He is going to come off and be replaced by Scanlon.

Leeds have come from 2-0 down to lead 3-2 in Chicago. Aaronson’s cross from the left side of the box should be cleared by Jones but he does not put his foot through it. Instead, that allows Longstaff to slot home past Mamardashvili. Leeds have scored three goals in a quarter of an hour.

Leeds are on level terms. A long throw from Ampadu out on the left is flicked on at the near post and Calvert-Lewin has the easiest of tap-ins at the back post. Liverpool were in cruise control at 2-0 up at the break but not have not been at it since half-time.

Justin is played in behind down the left channel and tries to pick out Calvert-Lewin in the centre of the box but Ndiaye steps in with a crucial interception.

Andoni Iraola is going to make a quadruple change. Elliott, Ramsay, Ndiaye and Tsimikas all come on. Szoboszlai is one of those to head off and hands Jones the armband.

Liverpool were much the better side in the first half but have not really been at the races since the break.

Leeds punish Kerkez’s error and get a goal back. Kerkez gifts the ball away inside his own half and Ampadu picks up not far outside the Liverpool penalty area. He spots the run of Aaronson to his left and slides it into the American, who takes one touch before sliding it underneath Mamardashvili and into the Liverpool net.

Wilson is fouled down Leeds’ right and he will take the free-kick. The Welshman clips it in and picks out Calvert-Lewin, whose header goes well wide of the target.

Calvert-Lewin gets a touch past Ndukwe just inside the Liverpool half and drives towards the Liverpool penalty area. It is difficult to know whether it is a shot or a cross from Calvert-Lewin and the ball goes wide of the far post. Bogle did make a run towards the back post and was hoping Calvert-Lewin would pick him out.

Liverpool negotiate a couple of long throws and a corner from Leeds in quick succession.

After Ndukwe’s pass inside his own half is intercepted, Justin decides to shoot from range but Mamardashvili easily saves.

Liverpool have made a number of changes at the break, with Chiesa, Jones, Gravenberch and Koumas all coming on. It takes an absolute age for Leeds to re-emerge, with Liverpool coming back out from the tunnel nearly ten minutes before Leeds. What on earth is going on in the Leeds dressing room at the break? This is ridiculous from Leeds.

The second half begins more than 20 minutes after the first ended. To be exact, 23 minutes is the gap. Calvert-Lewin is one of a few changes at half-time for Leeds, as is former Liverpool man Wilson. We are back under way in Chicago.

Jeremie 🔗 Flo 😍 pic.twitter.com/kxwhYA845Q

Andoni Iraola said before the game that Florian Wirtz would play 45 minutes in his first game of pre-season so we can expect him and Alexander Isak to come off at half-time.

Stateside Reds enjoying the action 🤩 pic.twitter.com/hfwaLmi8xB

Possession: Liverpool 60%-40% LeedsShots: 5-6Shots on target: 3-2Corners: 1-3

The first half is brought to an end and Liverpool take a 2-0 lead into the break courtesy of goals from Chambers and Wirtz.

Szoboszlai clips a delightful cross from the right all the way to the back post, aiming to pick out the run of Kerkez. A goal-kick is given, with the referee deciding the last touch came off Kerkez, but the Hungarian left-back is not happy with that decision. The replays prove why as the last touch came off Bogle.

There will be four minutes of added time at the end of this first half due to the Gudmundsson injury in particular.

Leeds have been forced into one change in this half and they might be forced into another here. As Wirtz scored, two Leeds players collided, which has resulted in Ampadu staying down and receiving treatment. The Leeds captain though does seem to be ok after receiving some treatment.

It is a lovely team goal from Liverpool to take them 2-0 up around five minutes before half-time. Nyoni’s flat ball out to the right side of the box is volleyed first time back across the box by Frimpong. Wirtz runs onto the ball and, from the penalty spot, slots the ball home past Cairns.

After Nyoni makes an interception inside his own half, Liverpool counter. The ball is shifted out to the left, where Ngumoha drives at Bogle. Ngumoha’s step-over takes him past Bogle inside the Leeds penalty area and he drives the ball across the six-yard box but no-one in a Liverpool shirt is on hand to tap it in. Should Isak have done a better job to get on the end of that one? Possibly.

Szoboszlai, who loves scoring free-kick stunners, blasts the free-kick into the wall.

Gudmundsson’s day is indeed over and is replaced by Bornauw, which could see a shift for Leeds.

Ngumoha is brought down by Bogle inches outside the Leeds penalty area out on the left. It was very, very close to being a penalty but was just outside the box. Before the free-kick will be taken, Leeds look like they will be forced into a change as Gudmundsson has gone down clutching at his right hamstring.

For the second time in a few minutes, Rodon steps in with a crucial interception. Wirtz slides a pass through into the Leeds box on the left to pick out the run of Ngumoha. Just as Ngumoha was getting his shot away from around eight yards out, Rodon slides in to intercept. However, the offside flag goes up against Ngumoha anyway.

Wirtz and Isak link up really well inside the Leeds half, with the latter putting a touch beyond one Leeds defender and runs towards the Leeds penalty area. However, Rodon steps in with a crucial interception to take it off Isak.

Nmecha scored from long range for Leeds the other day against Sunderland and he is not far off adding another long-range goal to his pre-season tally. His effort from just outside the box is dragged just wide of Mamardashvili’s right post.

Frimpong drives forward from inside his own half and takes Liverpool through the Leeds half before he is cynically pulled down by Tanaka, who is rightly booked. Sometimes in a pre-season friendly players might get away with that but this referee does not show mercy to Tanaka.

That is nearly a horror moment for Cairns in the Leeds goal. He rolls the ball out from his own box and Isak just about gets a touch on it but fortunately for Leeds it does not end in a horror show for Cairns.

Frimpong lays it across to Nyoni in a central position outside the box and the latter takes on the shot. Nyoni goes for accuracy over power and looks for the bottom corner but Cairns gets down to his left to make the save.

Chance for Leeds. Bogle whips in a cross from the right touchline and picks out the head of Nmecha, whose effort is saved well by Mamardashvili down to his right.

Liverpool hit the front in Chicago. Szoboszlai’s outswinger corner from the right is flicked on at the front post by Kerkez and is met by Chambers, who smashes home on the half volley into the Leeds net.

Liverpool counter from their own box after defending a long throw through Isak and Frimpong, whose cross from the right is deflected behind for the first corner of the game...

The pitch is not looking in the best condition, which perhaps is not a massive surprise when you consider that Chicago Fire played here last night. They beat Charlotte 2-1, with Robert Lewandowski scoring twice.

Gudmundsson is back to his feet after some treatment but is breathing quite heavily. It does appear that the Swedish wing-back should be fine to continue.

After Liverpool clear a Leeds long throw into the Liverpool penalty area, Gudmundsson goes down clutching at his lower back after an awkward landing and play is halted.

We are under way at Soldier Field. It is not too hot in Chicago today, with the temperature a touch over 20 degrees at kick-off.

Both sides emerge from the tunnel and we are just moments away from kick-off at Soldier Field in Chicago. You’ll Never Walk Alone rings around the stadium as the teams emerge.

Liverpool: Mamardashvili; Frimpong, Ndukwe, Chambers, Kerkez; Nyoni, Szoboszlai, Wirtz; Morrison, Isak, Ngumoha.Substitutes: Woodman, Davies, Chiesa, Jones, Elliott, Tsimikas, Gravenberch, Abe, Ramsay, Scanlon, McConnell, Koumas, Ndiaye, Wright, Sonni-Lambie.

Leeds: Cairns; Justin, Muharemovic, Rodon; Bogle, Ampadu, Stach, Tanaka, Gudmundsson; James, Nmecha.Substitutes: Mahady, Ombang, Lane, Lienou, Cresswell, Bornauw, Crew, Longstaff, Aaronson, Gnonto, Pickles, Wilson, Chadwick, Mills, Calvert-Lewin, Piroe.

There was a lot to take in, during those madcap 42 seconds, but it was a scene that showed the full extent of the issues Andoni Iraola must address.

First came a handshake with Curtis Jones that the midfielder, lost in red mist, barely acknowledged. It was not impressive, shrugging off a new manager like that, but as Iraola strode across the field at Yankee Stadium, after Liverpool’s 1-0 win over Wrexham on Wednesday, the action really began.

Jones squawked and jabbed at his arm. Dominik Szoboszlai bellowed back, arms stretched out so wide you could not help but notice. Next came Kostas Tsimikas throwing the captain’s armband on the floor, landing at Jones’s feet, as Giorgi Mamardashvili and Jeremie Frimpong looked on awkwardly.

The French defender, who has arrived from Rennes this summer, is not involved for Liverpool today and is yet to feature for his new club so far this pre-season as he is eased in after a shoulder injury days after his move to Liverpool was confirmed earlier this year.

Soldier Field in Chicago hosts an all-Premier League tie encounter as Liverpool take on Leeds as both sides bring their US tours to a close. Both Premier League encounters between these sides last season ended in draws; a 3-3 draw at Elland Road was followed up by a 0-0 stalemate at Anfield. The draw at Elland Road was immediately followed by Mohamed Salah speaking to the media, claiming he had been thrown under the bus.

It is a new era at Liverpool as former Bournemouth boss Andoni Iraola has replaced Arne Slot at Anfield. They kicked off the Iraola era in Nashville, Tennessee, with a 4-2 win over Sunderland, following that up with another victory in New York on Wednesday night, beating Wrexham 1-0, and will be aiming to make it three wins from three on their US tour.

“I think it [the US tour] has been really, really useful,” Iraola said in an interview on the official Liverpool website. Obviously, you spend a lot of time with the players, with the staff, you get all the information you can. And I think there is also an evolution, it has to be. We start to understand each other better, what we need to do. Every game, I hope we can get closer and closer and put ourselves in a position where the few players that still are not here start to train also, they are helped by the others.”

Virgil van Dijk and Cody Gakpo resumed training back on Merseyside whilst Alexis Mac Allister, Alisson and Victor Munoz are yet to return to training following their World Cup exploits. The trio of Florian Wirtz, Alexander Isak and Ryan Gravenberch are all set to feature for the first time this pre-season.

Leeds’ pre-season campaign began with a 3-2 loss to Championship Wrexham in Tampa, Florida before beating Sunderland 1-0 in New Jersey courtesy of a long-range strike from Lukas Nmecha. Former Liverpool man Harry Wilson joined Leeds on a free from Fulham this summer.

“Really tough but that is expected,” Wilson said. That is what pre-season is for, building up a base for when the season starts, making sure you are in the best physical position you can be to attack the season. It has been good. I played against them [Leeds] twice last year when I was at Fulham. Both games were really, really tough games.

“I think when the fans have got a good team to support, I think that [the atmosphere at Elland Road] goes up a notch. I think the size of the club was a massive part of me coming. Then speaking to the guys, the chairman, the sporting director, and seeing kind of the plans and the aims for the club, it is something I wanted to be a part of.”

#1869. Espanyol vs Deportivo La Coruna - prediction, team news, lineups

By Matt Law | 05 Nov 2026 15:31, Last updated: 05 Nov 2026 15:33

Deportivo La Coruna will be aiming to make it three straight wins in all competitions when they continue their La Liga campaign against Espanyol on Saturday afternoon.

The visitors will enter the match off the back of a 2-1 victory over Osasuna, while Espanyol recorded an impressive 1-0 win over Villarreal last time out.

Espanyol boast a record of three wins, two draws and six defeats from their 11 league matches this season, with 11 points leaving them in 14th spot in the La Liga table.

The White and Blues had been on a three-game losing run ahead of their clash with Villarreal last time out, including a shock 4-3 defeat to fourth-tier outfit Sestao in the Copa del Rey.

A second-half goal from Leandro Cabrera secured a valuable three points away to the Yellow Submarine, and it proved to be the perfect introduction for new head coach Eder Sarabia, although first-team coach Sergio Garcia took the team for that particular contest.

Espanyol just about lead the overall head-to-head record between these two sides, posting 39 wins to Deportivo's 35, but their last meeting ended in a goalless draw in February 2018.

The Catalan outfit are actually unbeaten against Deportivo since September 2015, winning three and drawing two of the last five meetings between the two sides.

Deportivo have not been victorious away to Espanyol since June 2007, meanwhile, which is an indication of the size of their task in this contest.

The Blue and Whites, who finished second in last season's Segunda Division to secure a return to the top flight, are currently eighth in the La Liga table, boasting a record of three wins, five draws and three defeats to collect 14 points.

Antonio Hidalgo's side recorded a 3-0 victory over Auriense in the Copa del Rey at the end of October before opening November with a 2-1 win over Osasuna in La Liga.

Deportivo will now take on Espanyol and Alaves either side of the November international break, before finishing the month with the small matter of a home fixture against Barcelona.

This will be Sarabia's first match in charge, and it could be a case of same again in terms of the team given the nature of the performance and result against Villarreal.

Roberto Fernandez has scored seven times in 12 appearances this season, and the 24-year-old is set to continue in the final third of the field.

As for Deportivo, Bright Ede, Zakaria Eddahchouri and Marc Casado remain unavailable for selection, but Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang is now back in the fold, coming off the bench in the clash with Osasuna after six games out injured.

Aubameyang has scored five goals in eight league appearances this season but is again expected to feature as a substitute rather than being introduced into the starting XI given that Bil Nsongo has two goals in his last three appearances.

Adama Traore is again expected to feature off the bench for the visitors this weekend after impressing in the second half of the Osasuna fixture.

#1868. Manchester United manager search takes major twist as new Michael Carrick details emerge

Didier Deschamps has reportedly turned down an approach over the Manchester United manager’s job, as more details emerge over the future of Michael Carrick.

Carrick’s position at Old Trafford has been subject to severe scrutiny for several weeks now following a miserable eight-game winless run across all competitions that was the club’s worst since the 1988/89 season.

Such a dire sequence was only snapped on Tuesday night as Man Utd staged an incredible turnaround following an abysmal first half to beat depleted Roma 3-2 at home in the Champions League, though it remains to be seen how much respite that offered their beleaguered head coach.

Sky Sports report that there remains support for Carrick within the United hierarchy, who have been said to be split on a potential replacement amid strong links to the likes of former Newcastle boss Eddie Howe and ex-Germany manager Julian Nagelsmann.

However, Sunday’s visit of Aston Villa to Old Trafford is likely to prove crucial before another review of the situation, with United having won just one of their opening nine games in the Premier League this term - at home to newly-promoted Ipswich back in August - as they go into the final weekend before the November international break sitting 17th in the table and outside of the relegation zone on goal difference only.

Villa are led by Unai Emery, who has also been linked with United but is expected now to sign a new long-term contract at Villa Park.

In a shock further twist to the saga, it was initially claimed in France on Thursday that Deschamps had been approached about potentially succeeding Carrick.

The 58-year-old is currently out of work after his successful 14-year spell in charge of the French national team - which included several major finals and one World Cup triumph - ended following the summer tournament, when he stood down after the expiration of his contract and was replaced by Zinedine Zidane.

However, it has since been reported by multiple outlets that Deschamps has indicated that he would have no interest in taking the United job as things stand, instead preferring to wait to likely return to football next summer.

United are not believed to be keen to appoint another interim manager if they do decide to part ways with Carrick, who was appointed to the full-time job in the summer on the strength of his success as a caretaker over the second half of last season following the sacking of Ruben Amorim in January.

#1866. Tottenham 'retain clause' in Harry Kane contract after Ballon d'Or win and new Bayern Munich deal

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau

Tottenham's agreement with Bayern Munich over Harry Kane remains in place, despite the 2026 Ballon d'Or winner signing a new contract.

After weeks of speculation, it was announced on Thursday that Kane has committed his future to Bayern until the summer of 2029 and reportedly becoming the highest-paid player in Europe by base salary.

Kane's new deal comes hot on the heels of winning the 2026 Ballon d'Or award over Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal, though he is now targeting more team success with the Bundesliga giants.

“We signed the contract yesterday, but the decision was made quite a long time ago," he said. "As I’ve said before, I know I’m part of a great team, that we’re competing for the Champions League and for every title.

"It’s important for me to be somewhere where I can improve. There’s no doubt about that here. My family is happy that we can stay here – overall, everyone’s happy.”

While Kane is happy and settled in Germany, a return to England with Tottenham at some point in the future has not completely ruled out following the new contract - even if there is currently no suggestion of this scenario materialising.

Spurs have confirmed that as part of Kane's move to Bayern in 2023, they negotiated a clause allowing them to match any bid made for the striker.

However, it was recently suggested by transfer journalist Fabrizio Romano that Bayern were looking at removing such clause which would have all-but ruled out a return to the Premier League for Kane.

Now, Telegraph Sport have reported that Spurs retained their first-option matching rights for the England captain.

As such, should Bayern - who are said to currently view Kane as “untouchable” - agree to sell the striker before his new contract expires, Tottenham would have to decide whether to match the bid in order to give the striker a decision to make.
